# Intake Brief — Herdr downtime worker: find work items in the tab's working directory; 60-min pause when none found

## Problem statement

The Herdr downtime worker (local-LLM idle dispatch) selects its next work item via `wl next --stage intake_complete|idea`, but those calls run **without** the `--worklog-dir` override the worklist uses, so they always resolve against the plugin process's own cwd (ContextHub) instead of the folder the user is currently working in (e.g. SorraAgents). As a result, downtime dispatch only ever picks items from the ContextHub backlog, even when the Herdr tab is browsing another project. Additionally, when no suitable items exist, the worker keeps polling and attempting dispatch on every idle period — the user wants it to stop looking for downtime entirely for 60 minutes.

## Users

- **Developer working on multiple projects** (e.g. SorraAgents, ContextHub): Opens a Herdr worklist tab in a project other than ContextHub, and wants the automatic downtime worker to fill idle LLM time from *that* project's backlog — not ContextHub's.
- **Developer with an empty/finished backlog**: When the current project has no suitable work items, wants the worker to stop burning cycles (proxy polling + `wl next` spawns) and back off for 60 minutes instead of retrying every idle period.

**User stories:**
- As a developer with a Herdr tab open in `/projects/SorraAgents`, I want downtime dispatch to select items from SorraAgents' worklog, so the idle LLM works on the project I'm actually in.
- As a developer whose current project has no work items available, I want the downtime worker to pause for 60 minutes, so it doesn't repeatedly query the proxy and spawn `wl` processes for an hour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The downtime worker's `wl next --stage intake_complete|idea` selection resolves against the **same worklog root the worklist uses** (the tab's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`-resolved root, via the existing `--worklog-dir` override). Verified by a test that asserts `--worklog-dir` is passed to `wl next` when the override is set, and by the live behavior: a SorraAgents tab dispatches an `SA-…` item, never a `WL-…` item.
- [ ] The downtime dispatch audit trail (`wl comment add` in `recordDispatch`) also targets the resolved worklog root (same `--worklog-dir` fix), so the auto-dispatch comment lands on the item in its own project's DB (currently it silently fails for non-ContextHub items).
- [ ] When both `wl next --stage intake_complete` and `wl next --stage idea` return no candidate, the worker enters a **60-minute cooldown (new setting, default 3,600,000 ms)** during which `tick()` performs no proxy polling, no idle tracking, and no dispatch. Cooldown is triggered only by a genuine "no candidate" outcome — never by transient `wl` errors (which continue to fail closed to "busy") or by an in-flight dispatch guard.
- [ ] After the cooldown expires, the worker resumes polling; the idle tracker requires a fresh full idle period before the next dispatch (no stale idle credit from before the pause).
- [ ] The new setting is clamped and persisted with the other downtime settings; a live settings change takes effect on the next tick (settings re-read each tick, matching existing behavior).
- [ ] The worklist header no longer shows a stale `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` during the pause; it reflects the paused state (e.g. `[downtime paused]`) so the UI is honest about the worker not looking.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: cooldown entry/exit, no poll during cooldown, no cooldown on transient error or in-flight guard, clamp behavior, `--worklog-dir` forwarding on `wl next` and `wl comment add`, and the header paused render.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and the plugin docs/settings reference (e.g. `packages/herdr/shared/README.md`) — the new `downtimeNoCandidateCooldownMs` setting must be documented.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not change the worklist's own (working) worklog-root resolution — only the downtime worker's `wl` invocations.
- Must not modify files outside the ContextHub repository (`.pi/`, `skill/`, etc.).
- Fail-closed behavior must be preserved: every boundary (wl failure, proxy timeout, audit failure) must never throw or crash the worker.
- Follow the existing test-first/injectable-seam patterns in `packages/herdr/src` (fixtures, `setExecFileAsync`, injected `DowntimeSpawn`).
- The 60-minute value is a default, not a hardcoded constant — it must be a new setting with a sane floor so the pause cannot be accidentally disabled or set trivially small.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `main()` resolves the tab's worklog root via `configureWorklogTarget(resolvedCwd)` and installs the `--worklog-dir` override with `setWorklogDir()`. The worklist's `fetchNextItems()` runs `wl` through `runWl()` which prepends `--worklog-dir`, so the list is correct.
- `createDowntimeDeps.getNextItem()` bypasses that seam: it calls `getExecFileAsync()('wl', ['next', '--stage', stage, '--json'])` directly — no `--worklog-dir` — so `wl next` resolves against the plugin process cwd (ContextHub). Verified live: from ContextHub cwd `wl next --stage intake_complete` returns `WL-0MSGI7UIH008USVB`; with `--worklog-dir /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog` it returns `SA-0MSI51QTA009WDFO`.
- `recordDispatch` (audit comment) has the same gap: `wl comment add` without `--worklog-dir` fails silently for non-ContextHub items (the `catch` swallows it, so the durable trail is lost).
- `claimItem` is already correct — it routes through `claimWorkItem()` → `runWl()` which applies the override.
- `createDowntimeWorker.tick()` currently: poll → evaluate idle → track → (threshold met) → dispatch; a `no-candidate` outcome just returns `{ dispatched: false, reason: 'no-candidate' }` and the next idle period retries. There is no cooldown/backoff state.
- Header status (`renderDowntimeStatus` in `worklist.ts`) renders from `worker.dispatching / enabled / idleSince`; during a full pause `idleSince` would be stale and the header would misreport "idle m:ss".

## Desired change

1. **Worklog-root routing (bug fix):** Route the downtime worker's `wl next` and `wl comment add` invocations through the same `--worklog-dir` override as the worklist (e.g. reuse the fetcher seam or prepend `--worklog-dir` from `getWorklogDir()`). Dispatch then selects and audits items from the folder the user is working in.
2. **60-minute cooldown (feature):** Add setting `downtimeNoCandidateCooldownMs` (default `3_600_000`; clamp with a floor, e.g. 60,000 ms). In `createDowntimeWorker`, when `dispatchDowntimeWork` returns `no-candidate`, set a `cooldownUntil` timestamp; while `now < cooldownUntil`, `tick()` returns immediately (no poll, no track, no dispatch). On cooldown entry, reset the idle tracker so a fresh full idle period is required after the pause. Expose the paused state on the worker so the header can render it.
3. **Tests + docs:** Unit tests for cooldown and `--worklog-dir` forwarding; update the header renderer and its tests; document the new setting.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — cooldown state (`cooldownUntil`) in `createDowntimeWorker`; early-return in `tick()`; reset idle tracker on pause; `clampDowntimeNoCandidateCooldownMs` + `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_NO_CANDIDATE_COOLDOWN_MS`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — expose the `--worklog-dir`-aware `wl` seam (e.g. a small `runWl`/`buildWlArgs` helper) so `index.ts` can reuse it.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps.getNextItem()` and `recordDispatch()` use the seam / `getWorklogDir()` so `wl next` and `wl comment add` target the resolved root.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new `downtimeNoCandidateCooldownMs` key + default + clamp wiring.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `renderDowntimeStatus` paused branch (e.g. `[downtime paused]`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` / `index.test.ts` / `settings.test.ts` / `worklist.test.ts` — new tests (cooldown lifecycle, no-cooldown-on-error, clamp, `--worklog-dir` forwarding, header paused render).
- Docs: `packages/herdr/shared/README.md` or plugin docs for the new setting.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS6AU1PI0076GYB** (completed) — "Herdr plugin should operate from Herdr tab working directory, not ContextHub": fixed the worklist's cwd resolution (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, `resolveWorklogRoot`, `setWorklogDir`); the downtime worker was not covered by that fix — this item completes the gap.
- **WL-0MS6LOUP5003GWNE** (completed) — SPIKE on how Herdr communicates tab cwd to plugins; evidence base for `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`.
- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** (completed) — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime": parent of the downtime worker itself (contract + wiring).
- **WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG** (open) — "Same-slot idle tracking for herdr downtime worker (per slot_id)": separate follow-up on per-slot identity; not blocking this item, but touches the same worker.
- **WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3** (in-progress) — "Central cache for wl read results to cut Herdr refresh spawn churn": the cooldown complements this by cutting `wl next` spawn churn during empty-backlog periods.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Changing `getNextItem` to always pass `--worklog-dir` could break a setup where the override is unset — mitigated: the seam only prepends the flag when the override exists (current behavior preserved otherwise).
- **Risk:** A too-long cooldown (user-configured) could starve the LLM of work after a project's backlog fills back up — mitigated by making it a setting with a documented default; the 60-min default matches the request.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Surfacing a richer paused-state UI (countdown, per-project status) is out of scope; only a minimal honest header label is included. Additional polish can be separate work items.
- **Assumption:** One plugin instance per Herdr tab/pane, so a per-worker cooldown is naturally per-project — no cross-tab coordination needed.
- **Assumption:** "No suitable items" == both `wl next --stage intake_complete` and `wl next --stage idea` return no candidate (the worker's existing selection semantics). The cooldown does NOT trigger on transient `wl`/CLI errors or proxy failures (user confirmed: "genuine only").
- **Assumption:** Cooldown = full pause (user confirmed: "pause completely") — no proxy polling or idle tracking during the 60 minutes.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "When no suitable items are found, should the worker pause completely for 60 minutes (no proxy idle polling, no idle tracking — a full stop), or keep monitoring LLM idle state and only skip the work-item lookup during the cooldown?" — Answer (user): "pause completely". Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q: "Should the 60-minute pause be a fixed constant, or a new downtime setting (like the existing downtimePollIntervalMs / downtimeIdleThresholdMs), defaulting to 60 minutes?" — Answer (user): "new setting". Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q: "Should the 60-minute pause apply only when the lookup genuinely returns no suitable items (both intake_complete and idea empty), or also on transient wl CLI errors (which currently fail closed to 'no dispatch')?" — Answer (user): "genuine only". Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q (internal, no user input needed): "Is the wrong-project selection a bug or a feature?" — Answer (agent): classified as `bug` (correctness fix for existing broken behavior) with a cooldown enhancement folded in; priority `critical` per user's explicit `--priority critical`. Source: intake analysis of `createDowntimeDeps` (packages/herdr/src/index.ts) + live `wl next` verification from both cwds.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQJL1W3X0055WJH** – Auto-refresh the Pi TUI browse selection list every 5 seconds (completed)
- **WL-0MM2FKKOW1H0C0G4** – Rebuild wl next algorithm (completed)

(`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) AND is the documented freshness gate reused by the
downtime dispatch audit tier (`selectAuditCandidate` /
`getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, which
treats `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` as "needs a fresh `/skill:audit`").

Running an audit itself bumps the work item's `updatedAt` to within a fraction
of a second of its `auditedAt` (`wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` +
the verdict-driven status transition). A freshness rule that requires a strict
gap on one side (e.g. only `auditedAt` comfortably ahead of `updatedAt`) can
therefore disagree with the just-persisted state. The canonical fix in
SorraAgents (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4) treats an audit as fresh when its
`auditedAt` is **at or near** the item's `updatedAt` (within a small
tolerance) because a near-simultaneous `updatedAt` bump is the audit's own
persistence write.

This item makes ContextHub's herdr audit-freshness logic follow the same
at-or-near rule so the icon display and the downtime dispatcher agree, and
never disagree on a just-persisted audit.

## Expected behaviour

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true (fresh) when `auditedAt`
  is at-or-near `updatedAt` within a small, named tolerance (the audit's own
  persistence write), and false otherwise.
- The icon (`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) shows the fresh icon for a
  just-persisted audit (no longer shows the stale glyph for an audit the run
  just persisted).
- The downtime audit candidate selection (`selectAuditCandidate` /
  `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`) uses the SAME
  `isAuditFresh` predicate, so a just-persisted fresh audit is NOT a dispatch
  candidate (no redundant `/skill:audit` re-run).
- Only one freshness definition exists; neither consumer re-implements its
  own comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditFresh` in `icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` at-or-near `updatedAt`
   (within a documented tolerance constant) as fresh, covering the
   audit-persistence case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the
   tolerance).
2. A unit test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` is true for a
   just-persisted audit (auditedAt and updatedAt differ by milliseconds).
3. A unit test asserts a genuinely stale audit (item updated well after the
   audit) is still false (stale), unchanged.
4. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`
   continue to use the imported `isAuditFresh` as the sole filter; a
   just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
5. Both consumers import the same helper; no competing freshness comparison
   is introduced in the dispatch or icon paths.

## Notes / Open questions

- `isAuditFresh` currently hard-codes a magic `60000` ms literal. Prefer
  naming a constant (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`) and routing
  both consumers through it.
- Reconcile the comparison shape of `isAuditFresh` (`auditTime > updateTime -
  buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics from the SorraAgents fix so
  both projects express the same intent. Confirm the target semantics with the
  operator before implementing.

## References

- discovered-from: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents audit_runner child
  freshness at-or-near fix) — canonical reference implementation.
- related-to: WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (Audit candidate selection),
  WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R (Audit dispatch tier), parent WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG.
data.title: Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher

# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

Build the test foundation for the event-driven path: a reusable in-memory herdr Unix-socket server (newline-delimited JSON-RPC) that answers `events.subscribe` with `subscription_started` and pushes scripted `{"data":{...},"event":"..."}` frames, plus TDD-red tests defining the `HerdrEventSubscriber` contract (connect/subscribe/dispatch/reconnect/fail-open).

## User story

As a developer, I want a deterministic mock of the herdr event socket so the subscriber, visibility gate and agent tracker can be tested without spawning real herdr processes.

- A reusable mock socket (net.createServer on a temp path, or an injectable connect seam) accepts `events.subscribe` requests with the documented subscription shape and replies `{"result":{"type":"subscription_started"}}`.

# events.ts: HerdrEventSubscriber socket module

Parent: Subscribe to herdr window events instead of polling active window status (WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ)

## Summary

New module `packages/herdr/src/events.ts` implementing `HerdrEventSubscriber`: a long-lived JSON-RPC-over-Unix-socket client that subscribes to herdr window events (global + per-pane), dispatches typed callbacks, reconnects with backoff, and fails open when the socket is unavailable.

## User story

As the worklist plugin, I want to receive herdr window events (pane focus/visibility, agent status changes, agent detected/closed/exited) pushed over the herdr socket instead of polling, so icons and visibility gating react immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Connects via `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` with fallback to `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`; unreachable socket → fail-open "events unavailable" (no throw, no unhandled rejection).
- Sends one `events.subscribe` request containing the global subscriptions (`pane.focused`, `pane.agent_detected`, `pane.closed`, `pane.exited`) plus a per-pane `pane.agent_status_changed` subscription for each pane currently tracked in `.worklog/agent-panes.json`.
- Parses newline-delimited JSON-RPC frames; dispatches typed callbacks for `pane_focused`, `pane_agent_status_changed`, `pane_agent_detected`, `pane_closed`, `pane_exited` (per verified live payload shape `{"data":{...},"event":"..."}`).
- Reconnects with backoff on socket errors (e.g. 500ms/1s/2s capped); transient errors never propagate to callers.
- `addPaneSubscription(paneId)` / `removePaneSubscription(paneId)` maintain per-pane subscriptions as panes appear/close.
- `close()` unsubscribes and closes the socket (no leaked connections).
- All F1 contract tests pass (mocked socket); live smoke check against the local herdr socket is optional but recommended.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `packages/herdr/src/events.ts` modelled on the JSON-RPC framing in `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py`.
- Typed event union + callback map; reconnect/backoff state machine; fail-open error surface.
- Wire env resolution (`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` → default path → poll fallback signal).

## Dependencies

- F1 (test harness/contract) — implementation makes the red tests green.

## Deliverables

- `events.ts` (new module) + green F1 tests + optional live smoke-check evidence comment.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/events.ts (new)
- packages/herdr/src/events.test.ts (new)
- packages/herdr/shared/grid.py (reference framing pattern)

Parent: Subscribe to herdr window events instead of polling active window status (WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ)

## Summary

Wire `pane_focused` events into the visibility gate: update `panePaused` immediately and trigger `doRefresh(true)` on hidden → visible transitions, making the 2s `resume-poll` a fallback-only task active only when the event path is unavailable.

## User story

As a user returning to a hidden tab, I want the worklist to refresh instantly and clear the `[paused — hidden]` indicator the moment the tab regains focus, without waiting for the next poll cycle.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `pane_focused` event for the current pane updates `panePaused` without a `herdr pane get` exec.
- A hidden → visible transition (tracked via `pane_focused`) triggers `doRefresh(true)` within 1s of the event; the `[paused — hidden]` indicator clears on the event, not on the next poll.
- The `resume-poll` scheduler task runs only while events are unavailable (fallback-only); the existing polling cadence is preserved when events are off.
- Integration tests (mock socket emitter) verify no `herdr pane get` exec occurs on the event path, and the existing worklist-visibility tests still pass.

# Wiring, fallback orchestration, lifecycle cleanup

Parent: Subscribe to herdr window events instead of polling active window status (WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ)

## Summary

Instantiate the `HerdrEventSubscriber` once per plugin instance in `index.ts`/`worklist.ts`, hand event callbacks to the visibility gate and agent tracker, add an events-health flag distinguishing "events active" from "polling fallback", and clean up (unsubscribe/close socket) on TUI exit — silently degrading to today's polling on any event-path failure.

## User story

As an operator, I want the event-driven path wired in safely: one subscriber per worklist instance, correct teardown, and zero behavioral regression when events are unavailable (older herdr, standalone mode, reconnect in progress).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The subscriber is instantiated exactly once per plugin instance and its callbacks are wired to `panePaused`/`doRefresh` (focus path) and `AgentTracker` (agent-status path); `close()` runs on TUI exit (no leaked socket connections).

- `min_herdr_version` stays conservative (0.7.0) with runtime degradation — the plugin still loads on herdr 0.7.0–0.7.4 and uses poll fallback (no manifest refusal).
- Integration tests pass: unreachable socket → poll fallback with no crash; TUI exit → socket closed; both event paths end-to-end with mocked emitter.

## Problem statement

SorraAgents is the canonical installer for pi agent guidance: its scripts/install_pi.sh symlinks the global guidance (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md -> ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md, plus skills and prompts) into every project. The global AGENTS.md already contains the full agent workflow (work-item lifecycle, implement/build-test-commit order, push policy, triage policy).

ContextHub's 'wl init' (src/commands/init.ts) currently has overlapping responsibilities: it prompts for a workflow choice (promptWorkflowChoice: N / B / M, where M is 'Manage custom workflow by editing AGENTS.md directly') and, via ensureWorkflowTemplateInstalled / insertWorkflowLoaderIntoAgents, can inline WORKFLOW content into the project's AGENTS.md. When the SorraAgents global install is present this creates two sources of truth for agent workflow guidance and can conflict with the canonical global file.

## User story

As a developer running wl init on a machine with the SorraAgents install, I want wl init to delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup to the SorraAgents install so the global guidance is the single source of truth and the project AGENTS.md only carries project-specific content.

## Desired change

- When the SorraAgents global install is detected (i.e. ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md resolves to a SorraAgents AGENTS_GLOBAL.md symlink), wl init should NOT inline workflow content into the project AGENTS.md. Instead it should emit/keep the canonical reference structure used by SorraAgents projects:
  - '## Global agent guidance' section referencing ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md
  - '## Project-specific guidance' section for local rules
- wl init should either invoke the SorraAgents install (scripts/install_pi.sh) or clearly document that the SorraAgents install is the canonical mechanism, rather than duplicating guidance.
- The existing pointer-line behavior from 'wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md pointer' (WL-0MLD6N0GW12MNKK0) must be preserved and aligned with the canonical structure above.
- Standalone Worklog users without the SorraAgents install keep the current workflow options (N/B/M) unchanged.

## Success criteria

1. With the SorraAgents global install present, running wl init in a fresh project does not inline WORKFLOW content into AGENTS.md; the file carries the canonical global-reference structure only.
2. wl init output/help documents the SorraAgents install as the canonical global-guidance mechanism (delegation), with no duplicated workflow content.
3. Without the SorraAgents install, existing wl init workflow behavior (N/B/M) is unchanged and existing tests pass.
4. Tests cover both environments (with and without the global SorraAgents symlink).
5. Full ContextHub test suite passes.

## Related work

- ContextHub: 'wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md pointer' (WL-0MLD6N0GW12MNKK0, completed) established the pointer-line behavior this item extends.
- SorraAgents: 'AGENTS.md installer: emit single reference line for new projects' is the complementary installer-side item; the AGENTS.md split (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md canonical source + symlink install) landed in SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W.

# Herdr selection list: gate background/foreground sync on DB-update check before spawning wl commands

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list spawns a burst of `wl` CLI processes on a fixed cadence — background `wl sync` every 60s plus a full refresh (`wl next`, 2× `wl list` mandatory subsets, expanded-children fetches) on every 30s auto-refresh tick — **regardless of whether the worklog database changed**. When the pane is idle (no agents writing, no remote activity), each cycle wastes 3–5 process spawns and a full git sync round-trip for zero visible change.

## Users

- **Herdr users running the selection list with auto-refresh/auto-sync on** — want the list to stay current without constant background `wl` process churn (spawn overhead, git fetch/pull/merge/push, lock contention with other panes).
- **Multi-pane / multi-agent setups** — the reduction in unnecessary `wl sync` invocations reduces lock-storm pressure between panes and cross-process DB churn.

Example user stories:
- As a Herdr user with an idle backlog, I want the selection list to avoid spawning any `wl` commands when nothing changed, so my machine isn't churning processes and git round-trips every 30–60s.
- As a Herdr user, I want background sync to still run at least once per configurable window (default 60s) even when nothing changed locally, so I still receive remote changes pushed by other machines.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On an auto-refresh tick, when the worklog DB has not changed since the last refresh cycle, the pane spawns **zero** `wl` processes for that tick (no `wl next`, no `wl list`, no children fetches, no `wl sync`, no action-count fetch).
2. On an auto-sync tick, `wl sync` is skipped when (a) the DB has not changed since the last cycle **and** (b) the last successful sync is fresher than the configurable max-staleness cap (default 60s). If either condition fails, the sync runs (subject to the existing heartbeat / single-flight / `--if-idle` guards).
3. The max-staleness cap is configurable via the Herdr settings file (e.g. new `maxSyncStalenessMs` setting, default `60000`), clamped to a sane minimum like the sync interval clamp.
4. Manual user actions — `S` (sync) and `r` (refresh) keypresses — always run, ignoring the gate.
5. The very first cycle after pane start always runs (no prior "last seen" signal), and any failure to read the DB-change signal fails **open** (the cycle runs), so the list can never go stale due to a signal-read error.
6. The existing cross-instance heartbeat (`last-sync-time`), single-flight, and `--if-idle` guards remain in place for syncs that do run.
7. Unit tests cover: gate skip/run decisions for refresh and sync ticks (changed/unchanged DB, stale/fresh last-sync, manual override, first-cycle, fail-open), plus the new setting's parse/clamp behavior.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The Herdr plugin package (`packages/herdr`) has **zero npm dependencies** and intentionally duplicates small shared helpers per TUI (decision Q2c in WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B) — a small pure helper duplicating the counter-read logic is consistent with this pattern.
- The DB-change signal must be cheap (a file read or two) and must NOT spawn a `wl` process itself — that is the whole point of the gate.
- The signal must be cross-process stable: the wl CLI read cache (F2) deliberately avoids SQLite file mtimes because "the SQLite files are rewritten by the app on every open/close cycle… file-based fingerprints are not stable across processes" (`src/read-cache.ts`). The gate must not produce false "changed" signals from the pane's own reads.
- Do not change wl CLI sync behavior itself; the incremental-sync work (WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q) is separate scope.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `runWorklistTui` registers two scheduler tasks: `refresh` (every `refreshIntervalMs`, default 30s, always calls `doRefresh(false)` → spawns read commands) and `sync` (every `syncIntervalMs`, default 60s, calls `doSync(true, heartbeatTtlMs)` then `doRefresh(false)`). Plus a `resume-poll` task that calls `doRefresh(true)` on hidden→visible transition.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — `runSync` spawns `wl sync` fire-and-forget with cross-instance heartbeat skip (`last-sync-time` marker, `isSyncHeartbeatFresh`), single-flight guard, and `--if-idle`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — all read commands (`wl next`, `wl list`, children, action-count) go through `runWl`; the CLI serves many from its on-disk read cache (F2), but a process spawn still occurs per command.
- `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — the wl CLI maintains a monotonic per-worklog-dir **state counter** (`~/.cache/wl/state/<sha256(worklogDir)>.json`, `{ "state": N }`), bumped by every wl write command and by post-sync invalidation (`invalidateCacheForWrite`). This is the natural "DB changed" signal: cross-process, stable across reads, and already the CLI's freshness authority.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — typed settings JSON with clamped intervals; `syncIntervalMs` has a 60s minimum clamp.
- Manual `S`/`r` keypresses dispatch to `doSync()` / `doRefresh(true)` unconditionally.

## Desired change

- Add a small pure module in `packages/herdr` (e.g. `db-change.ts`) that:
  - resolves the wl cache dir (mirroring `resolveCacheDir()` precedence: `WL_CACHE_DIR` → `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/wl` → `~/.cache/wl`);
  - reads the state counter for the resolved worklog dir (`state/<sha256(worklogDir)>.json`), returning the counter value (0 when absent); and
  - exposes a `DbChangeTracker`/helper that remembers the last-seen counter per pane and answers `dbChangedSinceLastCycle()` (fail-open: any read error ⇒ true).
- Gate the scheduler tasks in `runWorklistTui`:
  - `refresh` tick: skip (spawn nothing) when the DB is unchanged since the last cycle.
  - `sync` tick: skip `wl sync` when DB unchanged **and** last successful sync (heartbeat marker) is within the configurable max-staleness cap; otherwise run `doSync` + `doRefresh` as today.
  - `resume-poll` hidden→visible transition: apply the same DB-change gate (list content is identical when nothing changed).
  - Manual `S`/`r` paths unchanged (always run).
- Add the configurable cap to settings (e.g. `maxSyncStalenessMs`, default 60s, clamped ≥1s or aligned with the sync-interval clamp) and pass it through `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`.
- Keep all existing guards (heartbeat, single-flight, `--if-idle`) for syncs that do run.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts` — NEW: pure DB-change signal reader (wl cache-dir resolution + state-counter read + last-seen tracker), fail-open.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — expose/adapt staleness helpers (reuse `readSyncHeartbeatMs`) so the sync tick can decide "DB unchanged AND sync fresh ⇒ skip".
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — wire the gate into the `refresh` / `sync` / `resume-poll` scheduler tasks; manual `S`/`r` untouched.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new `maxSyncStalenessMs` setting (default `60000`) with clamping.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the new setting into `runWorklistTui`.
- `src/read-cache.ts` — read-only reference for the counter-file format/path derivation (no changes expected).
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/db-change.test.ts` (NEW), plus updates to `auto-sync.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts`.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W` — Cross-instance sync heartbeat (F3): the `last-sync-time` marker and heartbeat TTL this change composes with. Completed.
- `WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E` — wl sync lock storm: auto-sync single-flight / `--if-idle` guards; gating reduces spawn pressure further. Completed.
- `WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA` — wl CLI read cache (F2) with the state-counter fingerprint this gate reuses as its signal. Completed.
- `WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q` — Incremental sync: only export/push changed work items (CLI-side; explicitly out of scope here). Open.
- `WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B` — Smart-selection duplication decision (Q2c): precedent for duplicating a small pure helper into the Herdr package. Completed.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — release workflow (no code impact; doc reference).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Remote-pull latency (accepted tradeoff, user-confirmed):** skipping `wl sync` when the DB is unchanged delays pulling remote changes until the next sync that does run. Bounded by the max-staleness cap (default 60s) so remote freshness is never worse than the cap.
- **Signal completeness:** the state counter is bumped by wl CLI writes and post-sync invalidation. External tools writing the SQLite DB directly (not via wl) would not bump it — mitigated by the staleness cap, which forces a periodic sync regardless. Assumed acceptable.
- **Configurable cap naming/units:** `maxSyncStalenessMs` in ms, default 60000, clamped to ≥1s (aligned with `heartbeatTtlForInterval`'s clamp) — exact name subject to implementer/plan review.
- **Scope-creep guard:** incremental sync (WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q), event-driven window subscription (WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ), and WAL checkpointing (WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I) are tracked separately and must NOT be pulled into this work item.
- **Behavioral parity:** when the DB IS changing, cadence must match today (no additional latency); only the no-change case adds skipping.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (asked 2026-08-07): "If the local DB hasn't changed, should the background `wl sync` also be skipped? That means remote changes pushed by other machines would only be pulled when local activity bumps the counter (or via manual `S`). Acceptable — or should the sync path stay ungated while only the refresh reads are skipped?" — Answer (user): "Partially acceptable. wl sync can be skipped if no local DB changes. However, it should not go more than 1 minute (configurable) without being run." Source: interactive reply. → Implemented as AC2/AC3: sync is gated by (DB unchanged AND last successful sync within configurable max-staleness cap, default 60s).
- Q2 (asked 2026-08-07): "Should manual refresh (`r`) and manual sync (`S`) always run regardless of the check? (My assumption: yes — user-initiated actions always execute.)" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply. → Implemented as AC4.
- Q3 (asked 2026-08-07, /skill:find-related): "Which work items are related?" — Research: the find-related script (`find_related.py --work-item-id WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ`) resolved the wrong worklog store (SorraAgents framework repo) on both runs and returned unrelated items (OpenBrain submission, file-path convention, a-y shortcut). The matches were excluded per the skill's conservative policy (false negatives preferred); the curated Related work section above (verified via `wl show` against the ContextHub store) is authoritative.

# Intake Brief: Colour code work items by priority in selection lists (CLI + Herdr)

**Work Item ID:** WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6

**Headline:** Colour coding of work items in the selection list should be based on **priority**, not stage: critical are red, low are dimmed, medium is white, high is orange — recorded in a shared theme file.

## Problem Statement

Work item titles in selection lists are currently coloured by **stage** (progression: gray → blue → cyan → yellow → green → white, from WL-0MQ53H78W000DQ08). Stage progression communicates workflow position, but operators scanning a list need to see **priority** at a glance — critical items should jump out in red, low-priority items should recede. The colour scheme must be defined once in a shared theme file.

## Users

All Worklog users viewing work item lists:

- **Operators and agents** scanning `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent` need immediate visual cue of what matters (critical = red, high = orange).
- **Herdr users** browsing the Worklog selection list pane need the same priority cue.

Example user stories:
- "As an operator, I want critical work items to appear red so I can immediately spot what needs attention."
- "As an agent, I want low-priority items dimmed so they recede while scanning the list."
- "As a project manager, I want a consistent priority colour scheme across the CLI and the Herdr selection list, defined in one shared theme file."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The canonical priority colour mapping is recorded in the shared theme file `src/theme.ts`:
   - `critical` → red
   - `high` → orange
   - `medium` → white
   - `low` → dimmed
2. Work item **titles** are coloured by priority and work item **ids** are coloured by stage, everywhere they appear: `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl recent`, `wl show`, `wl next`, and the Herdr worklist selection list (`formatItemLine`).
3. Blocked items no longer receive the unconditional red override; they are coloured by their natural priority like every other item (per clarification Q3b).
4. Unknown/missing priority falls back to a sensible default colour (e.g. medium/white) and unknown/missing stage keeps a sensible default (gray) — matching current fallback behaviour.
5. Unit tests cover the new priority colour mapping and the title/priority + id/stage split in both the CLI helpers (`src/commands/helpers.ts`) and the Herdr icons (`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`), including blocked and unknown-priority cases.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr/`) is a separate package depending only on `@worklog/shared`; it renders raw ANSI 256-colour escape codes and cannot import `src/theme.ts` (which depends on chalk).
- The Pi-based TUI extension (`packages/tui/`) is **out of scope** — it is slated for removal (see WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N) and colours via Pi theme tokens, not the theme file.
- "Orange" should use a colour consistent with the existing `theme.text.readyNo` (`chalk.hex('#FFA500')`).
- No new dependencies.

## Existing state

- `src/theme.ts` already has a `priority` map (`critical: chalk.redBright`, `high: chalk.yellowBright`, `medium: chalk.blueBright`, `low: chalk.gray`), a `stage` progression map, and a `blocked: chalk.redBright` override.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `renderTitle()` colours the title by stage (`titleColorForStage`), with a blocked override checked first; `formatTitleAndId()` renders the id muted (`theme.text.muted`); `humanFormatWorkItem()` also renders ids muted in several formats.
- Herdr: `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` has `stageColor()` / `applyStageColour()`; `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `formatItemLine()` colours the title by stage and leaves the id uncoloured. `STAGE_COLORS` (worklist.ts) is reused by the stage-filter dialog and separators.

## Desired change

- **`src/theme.ts`:** update `priority` colours to red / orange / white / dim. Keep the `stage` map (now used for ids). Remove the `blocked` override (per Q3b) or leave it unused — implementer decision, but `renderTitle` must no longer apply it.
- **`src/commands/helpers.ts`:** `renderTitle()` colours by priority (fallback for unknown priority); `formatTitleAndId()` and `humanFormatWorkItem()` colour ids by stage instead of muted. This automatically covers list, search, recent, show, next.
- **Herdr `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`:** add `priorityColor(priority)` / `applyPriorityColour(text, priority)` using ANSI 256 codes (red ≈ 196, orange ≈ 208, white ≈ 15, dim ≈ 241). Keep `stageColor` / `applyStageColour` for ids.
- **Herdr `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:** `formatItemLine()` — title via priority colour, id via stage colour. Keep `STAGE_COLORS` for the stage filter dialog and separators.
- **Shared theme consideration:** the priority colour *spec* lives in `src/theme.ts`. To prevent drift between the CLI (chalk) and Herdr (ANSI), consider extracting a colour-name spec (e.g. a `packages/shared` module mapping priority → colour name, consumed by both) — at minimum the two maps must stay consistent. Flag as design decision for the implementer; do not over-engineer.

## Key Files:

- `src/theme.ts` — canonical priority colour mapping (red/orange/white/dim); stage map retained for ids
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `renderTitle` (priority colour), `formatTitleAndId` / `humanFormatWorkItem` (stage-coloured ids)
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — add `priorityColor` / `applyPriorityColour` (ANSI 256)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatItemLine` title/priority + id/stage split

## Related work

- **WL-0MQ53H78W000DQ08** (completed, high) — "Refactor colour mappings: remove status-based colours, use stage progression with blocked override". Established the current stage-based scheme this item replaces for titles. See `src/theme.ts`, `src/commands/helpers.ts`.
- **WL-0MQ8LKXH20058N1M** (completed, high) — "Consistent colour scheme for work item titles in Blessed and Pi TUIs". Earlier consistency work; Pi TUI out of scope here.
- **WL-0MP15YIQ200748RC / WL-0MP15YJ4A0031YGR** (completed) — "Implement colour mapping in TUI and CLI" and its test item.
- **WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N** (open, high) — "Remove the Pi-based TUI from the repo; keep the agent-side Pi plugin features" — Pi TUI excluded from this scope.
- **WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY** (open, high) — "Herdr selection list: sort by priority first, then stage" — sibling priority-related change to the same Herdr worklist.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Selection list" = `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent` / `wl show` outputs plus the Herdr worklist pane (confirmed by user: "both a and b plus the herdr plugin").
- **Assumption:** Title = priority colour, id = stage colour, everywhere (confirmed: "Always use priority in title and stage colouring in id (everywhere they appear)").
- **Assumption:** Blocked items show their natural priority colour; the always-red blocked override is removed (confirmed: Q3 answer "b").
- **Risk:** CLI and Herdr colour maps drifting apart → mitigate by keeping both maps in the shared theme spec / one source of truth.
- **Risk:** ANSI 256 approximations of "orange" / "white" / "dim" in Herdr may differ slightly from chalk's named colours → verify visually against the CLI.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Pi TUI colouring, sorting changes (WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY), and other Herdr list features are separate work items and must not be expanded into this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope of 'selection list' — should priority-based colours apply to (a) `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent`, (b) `wl show` detail view, (c) both?" — Answer (user): "both a and b plus the herdr plugin". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Priority vs Stage relationship — should priority (a) replace stage as primary colour source, (b) supersede only for title colour keeping stage in metadata, (c) only affect list views?" — Answer (user): "Always use priority in title and stage colouring in id (everywhere they appear)". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Blocked items — currently `blocked` is a red override that beats stage. Should blocked items (a) still override everything (always red), (b) show their natural priority colour?" — Answer (user): "b". Meaning: blocked items are coloured by their priority like every other item; the unconditional red override in `renderTitle` is removed. Source: interactive reply.

# Intake Brief: Fully remove deprecated icons.ts from all projects that use it (src + herdr)

**Work Item ID:** WL-0MSJ4BT4Z002HH9B

**Headline:** After the icons→theme merge (WL-0MSJ4BT4Z009LIB4), fully remove `icons.ts` from every project that uses it — `src/icons.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — rewiring all importers to the single shared theme source.

## Problem Statement

Once `src/icons.ts` becomes a deprecated wrapper and the herdr package still carries its own adapted copy (`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`), there remain duplicate/dead theme-icon artefacts. Both copies should be fully removed and all consumers should import from the single shared source (`theme.ts` / shared module), eliminating duplication and drift.

## Users

- **Maintainers** — one source of truth for icons/theme; no deprecated wrapper to keep in sync.
- **Herdr plugin maintainers** — herdr consumers import icons from the shared source instead of a local copy.

Example user stories:
- "As a developer, I want `icons.ts` gone so there is no deprecated path left to import from."
- "As a herdr maintainer, I want the local icons copy removed so icons can't drift from the main project."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `src/icons.ts` is deleted, and all of its former consumers are rewired to import from `src/theme.ts`:
   - `src/commands/helpers.ts`
   - `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` (imports move to `theme.ts`; test file may be renamed, e.g. `theme-icons.test.ts`, with content preserved)
2. `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` is deleted, and all herdr consumers are rewired to the shared source:
   - `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
   - `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
   - `packages/herdr/src/icons.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist-agent-state.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist-icons.test.ts`
3. After rewiring, the herdr package still builds and its full test suite passes; the worklist renders icons/colours identically (parity verified by existing herdr tests).
4. No file in the repo (excluding `node_modules`, `dist`, `.git`) imports from a removed `icons.js` path — verified by a repo-wide grep in CI or the test suite.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes; TypeScript build must succeed.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments, `docs/icons-design.md`, herdr README if it references the copy).

## Constraints

- **Prerequisite:** this item is blocked by WL-0MSJ4BT4Z009LIB4 (the merge + deprecation) — dependency edge recorded via `wl dep add`. Do not start until the merge is complete.
- Herdr is a separate package depending only on `@worklog/shared`; it cannot import `src/theme.ts` directly if that file depends on chalk (see open design question below).
- No behaviour changes to rendered output — icons/colours must render exactly as before the removal.
- No new third-party dependencies.

## Existing state

- After WL-0MSJ4BT4Z009LIB4: `src/icons.ts` = deprecated wrapper re-exporting from `src/theme.ts`.
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` = standalone adapted copy (icon maps + ANSI stage-colour functions `stageColor`, `applyStageColour`, `STAGE_COLORS` re-exported by `worklist.ts`).
- Consumers: `src/commands/helpers.ts`, `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` (src); `worklist.ts`, `downtime-worker.ts`, `worklist-agent-state.test.ts`, `icons.test.ts`, `worklist-icons.test.ts` (herdr).

## Desired change

- Delete `src/icons.ts`; update `helpers.ts` and the unit tests to import from `theme.js`.
- Delete `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`; update herdr consumers to import from the shared source.
- Resolve the herdr import path (see open question) — likely by keeping the icon/colour data as dependency-free constants consumable by herdr (e.g. via a `packages/shared` module or a chalk-free section of `theme.ts`).
- Add a repo-wide guard (grep-based test) asserting no stale `icons.js` imports remain.

## Key Files:

- `src/icons.ts` — deleted
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — import `theme.js` instead of `icons.js`
- `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` — imports move to `theme.ts` (file may be renamed)
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — deleted
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — import shared source
- `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` (icons, worklist-agent-state, worklist-icons) — imports updated
- `packages/shared/` (candidate) — shared icon/colour data module if herdr cannot import `theme.ts`

## Related work

- **WL-0MSJ4BT4Z009LIB4** (open, medium) — "Merge icons.ts into theme.ts as single source of truth; deprecate icons.ts wrapper". Blocks this item.
- **WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6** (open, medium) — "Colour code work items by priority in selection lists (CLI + Herdr)". Touches the same `theme.ts` priority/stage maps and herdr colour functions; the shared-source decision for herdr should align with it.
- **WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N** (open, high) — "Remove the Pi-based TUI from the repo" — the Pi TUI does not import `src/icons.ts`; out of scope.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "All projects that use it" = the main CLI (`src/`) and the herdr plugin package — confirmed by user ("both").
- **Assumption:** The herdr copy is removed in this item; its stage-colour functions move to the shared source rather than being deleted.
- **Risk:** Herdr cannot import `src/theme.ts` (chalk dependency) → open design question: extract dependency-free icon/colour data into `packages/shared` (herdr's existing dependency) or keep `theme.ts` chalk-free at the data layer. Must be resolved in planning before implementation.
- **Risk:** A missed importer leaves a dangling import and breaks the build → mitigated by the repo-wide grep guard (AC 4) and full suite.
- **Scope-creep guard:** No new icon/colour features here; this is removal and rewiring only.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Removal scope for the 'fully remove icons.ts' work item — should it cover (a) only `src/icons.ts`, or (b) also remove the herdr copy `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`?" — Answer (user): "both". Source: interactive reply.
- OPEN QUESTION (for planning): how do herdr consumers import the shared icon/colour content once `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` is deleted — direct import of `src/theme.ts` (requires chalk-free data layer), a new `packages/shared` module, or another mechanism? Decision should keep a single source of truth and align with WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6.

# Intake Brief: Merge icons.ts into theme.ts as single source of truth; deprecate icons.ts wrapper

**Work Item ID:** WL-0MSJ4BT4Z009LIB4

**Headline:** Merge the content of `src/icons.ts` into `src/theme.ts` so all theme content (colours + icons) comes from a single file; `src/icons.ts` becomes a deprecated re-export wrapper.

## Problem Statement

Theme/styling content is split across two files: `src/theme.ts` (chalk colour mappings) and `src/icons.ts` (emoji icon maps, text fallbacks, accessible labels, and icon functions). This split means consumers must know which file to import from, and the two files can drift in naming/style conventions. All theme content should come from a single file: `src/theme.ts`.

## Users

- **CLI developers** adding or changing visual elements (colours, icons) — one canonical file to edit.
- **Herdr plugin maintainers** — the herdr package carries its own adapted copy (`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`); a single-source merge is the prerequisite for later consolidating/removing copies (see WL-0MSJ4BT4Z002HH9B).

Example user stories:
- "As a developer, I want all theme and icon definitions in one file so I don't have to guess where a glyph or colour lives."
- "As a maintainer, I want `icons.ts` deprecated so its consumers can be migrated off it and the file removed."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All content from `src/icons.ts` is relocated into `src/theme.ts` — including the icon maps and public functions for priority, status, stage, risk, effort, epic, audit result, stale audit, and producer-review icons (icon + fallback + label variants) plus `iconsEnabled` and the `IconOptions` interface.
2. `src/theme.ts` is the single source of truth for both colour and icon content.
3. `src/icons.ts` becomes a thin wrapper that only re-exports from `src/theme.ts` and carries a `@deprecated` JSDoc marker instructing consumers to import from `theme.js` instead.
4. All existing consumers (`src/commands/helpers.ts`, `tests/unit/icons.test.ts`) keep working unchanged through the wrapper — no import rewiring in this item.
5. Unit tests cover: the wrapper re-exports the full original public API surface (parity), and `theme.ts` exports the icon functions with unchanged behaviour (emoji vs `noIcons` fallback).
6. The relocated icon maps remain pure data (no chalk dependency) so the herdr package can consume them in the follow-up removal item.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes; TypeScript build must succeed.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/icons-design.md`, and any README/docs entries referencing `src/icons.ts`.

## Constraints

- Public API of the icons module must be preserved exactly (all exported names and signatures) so the wrapper and downstream consumers are unaffected.

# Intake Brief: Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned

## Problem statement

When a pi agent pane is spawned from the Herdr worklist, its title is generic
("Pi Agent" for agent commands, "Command Output" for `!!`/`!` shell commands),
so the user cannot tell at a glance how each pane was spawned or which work
item it belongs to. The downtime dispatcher already names its panes
(`Downtime plan` / `Downtime intake` / `Downtime audit`), but the manual spawn
paths do not.

## Users

- **Herdr users running skill/workflow commands** — want pane titles that
  identify the spawn source (manual vs downtime), the skill invoked, and the
  target work item, so multi-pane sessions are navigable.
  - As a user, I trigger `/skill:implement <id>` from the worklist, and the
    new pane is titled `Manually triggered implement <title> - WL-<id>` so I
    can find it among other panes.
  - As a user running a `!!` shell shortcut (e.g. audit approve/reject), the
    resulting pane identifies the command and work item instead of a generic
    "Command Output".
  - As a user, I see downtime-dispatched panes in the same descriptive format
    so all pi panes follow one naming convention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Agent-command panes spawned from the worklist (skill shortcuts,
   `/intake`, `/plan`) get a descriptive title of the form
   `Manually triggered <skill> <work item title> - <id>`; the skill token is
   derived from the command (e.g. `/skill:implement` → `implement`).
2. Free-form `/prompt:` commands produce a title like
   `Manually triggered prompt <first words…>` (truncated), or a sensible
   fallback when no prompt text remains.
3. `!!`/`!` shell-command panes (routed via `run-in-pane.sh`) get a
   descriptive title instead of the generic "Command Output", identifying the
   command/work item where available.
4. Downtime-dispatched panes are updated from the short `Downtime <kind>` to
   the same full format (e.g. `Downtime triggered <skill> <title> - <id>`),
   keeping one consistent convention across all pi panes.
5. Title length is bounded (truncated) so pane names stay usable in the Herdr
   UI; commands without a work item still get a descriptive-but-safe title.
6. Unit tests cover title construction for each spawn path (manual skill,
   `/prompt:`, `!!`/`!` shell, downtime), including missing work-item and
   missing-title cases.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No change to the interactive `open-pi-agent.sh` pane (keeps "Pi Agent").
- The work-item title must be sourced without adding blocking process spawns
  in the TUI loop — prefer threading the already-loaded item title from the
  worklist state into the spawn path.
- Pane titles must remain safe for herdr pane-rename (no shell metacharacter
  injection; the rename already runs with quoting).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` supports `--pane-name` (default
  `Pi Agent`) and renames the pane after spawning pi.
- Manual agent dispatches go through `buildSendToPiArgs` in
  `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, which does **not** pass `--pane-name` →
  panes are named `Pi Agent`.
- The downtime worker (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) uses
  `buildDowntimePaneArgs` → `--pane-name "Downtime <kind>"`.
- `!!`/`!` shell commands route through `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh`
  which renames the pane `Command Output` (override via `RUN_IN_PANE_NAME`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `resolveAndRouteCommand` has the selected
  item (with `id` + `title`) at dispatch time, but `onCommand` only forwards
  `(command, model)`.

## Desired change

- Extend the agent-command spawn path (`buildSendToPiArgs` call site in
  `index.ts`) to pass `--pane-name` with a title built from a descriptor
  (`Manually triggered`), the skill name parsed from the command, the work
  item title, and the work-item ID.
- Thread the selected item's title from `worklist.ts` into the dispatch
  (extend the `onCommand` seam or pass a prebuilt title) so no extra `wl`
  spawn is needed.
- Add the same `--pane-name` behavior to the `!!`/`!` shell path
  (`run-in-pane.sh` invocation in `index.ts`), replacing "Command Output".
- Update `buildDowntimePaneArgs` / the downtime spawn to the full format so
  downtime panes match (e.g. `Downtime triggered <kind> <title> - <id>`).
- Centralize title construction (descriptor + skill + title + id, with
  truncation) so all spawn paths share one function.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — agent/pane dispatch; add `--pane-name` to
  `buildSendToPiArgs` and the `run-in-pane.sh` spawn.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `resolveAndRouteCommand` / `onCommand`
  seam; forward the selected item's title (or a prebuilt pane title).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `buildDowntimePaneArgs` / pane
  name; adopt the full format (`Downtime triggered …`).
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — pane-name plumbing if the title
  is passed via env/arg.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`
  — tests for the new title construction per spawn path.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9` — "Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item
  and show their status icon". Related: pane spawn plumbing (pane-id capture)
  in the same dispatch path.
- `WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG` — "Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items
  without a valid audit". Related: downtime audit tier uses the same
  `buildDowntimePaneArgs` path that will adopt the full title format.
- `WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K` — downtime worker (dispatch panes open in the
  resolved worklog root); pane naming originates here.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the work-item title is threaded from the worklist state
  (already loaded) rather than fetched via `wl show` — avoids extra spawns in
  the TUI loop. If threading proves invasive, fall back to `wl show` at spawn
  (documented tradeoff: extra subprocess per dispatch).
- **Risk:** long work-item titles make pane names unusable — mitigated by
  truncation (bounded length) in the shared title builder.
- **Assumption:** `/prompt:` panes use `Manually triggered prompt <first
  words…>` per user confirmation.
- **Assumption:** `!!`/`!` panes keep the manual descriptor with the command
  and work-item context; exact token order to be confirmed during planning.
- **Scope-creep guard:** interactive `open-pi-agent.sh` naming is explicitly
  out of scope; any further spawn-source descriptors discovered during
  implementation should be recorded as linked work items, not folded in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which panes should get descriptive titles? (a) Only agent-command
  panes spawned from skill shortcuts (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`,
  `/prompt:`), (b) also the `!!`/`!` shell-command panes (currently
  'Command Output'), (c) also the interactive `open-pi-agent.sh` pane
  (currently 'Pi Agent')?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **b** — agent-command panes AND the
    `!!`/`!` shell-command panes; the interactive open-pi-agent pane is
    excluded.
- Q2: "Should the downtime dispatcher's panes be updated to match the new
  full format (e.g. `Downtime triggered plan <title> - WL-<id>`), or keep its
  current short form (`Downtime plan`) while only the manual path gets the
  descriptive format?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **update** — downtime panes adopt the
    same full format for a single consistent convention.
- Q3: "Free-form `/prompt:` commands have no skill name and may have no
  work-item ID. What should their title be (e.g. `Manually triggered prompt
  <first words…>`), or should they keep the default 'Pi Agent'?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **use the suggested title**
    (`Manually triggered prompt <first words…>`).

---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I** – Detail view ToC for Related Docs (completed)
- **WL-0MMLXTBCH0F4NV3T** – Migrate GitHub helpers to use throttler (completed)
- **WL-0MMS4EVN10RG8T47** – Migration & Safety Flow (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-Herdr-pane-title-should-reflect-how-it-was-spawned-WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y.md` — matched: already, descriptors, dispatcher, downtime, end (+18 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSI4TAT70058921-rename-podcast-editing-tab-to-worklog/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: already, downtime, end, herdr, how (+14 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: already, downtime, end, herdr, how (+14 more)

# Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added

## Problem Statement

A parent work item cannot be `completed` (status) or `in_review` (stage) while it has uncompleted children — the invariant is "if any child is not completed, the parent cannot be completed". Today, `wl create --parent <id>` and `wl update <id> --parent <new-parent>` add children without re-examining the parent's lifecycle state, so a completed or in-review parent can silently end up with new, uncompleted children. The `wl close` command already has recovery logic for this state ("children were added after the parent was closed"), but nothing prevents it from arising in the first place.

## Users

- **Project managers / producers** who close a parent, then later realize a subtask was missed and add it as a child.
  - *As a project manager, I want adding a child to a completed parent to automatically reopen the parent for planning, so that the parent's lifecycle state always reflects that its subtree is not finished.*
- **Agents / automation** that add child work items during planning.
  - *As an agent, I want the parent's status/stage kept consistent automatically, so I don't have to remember to reset it manually.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a child is created with `wl create --parent <id>` and the parent's status is `completed` (stage `in_review` or `done`), the parent is automatically moved to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
2. When a child is created with `wl create --parent <id>` and the parent's stage is `in_review` (status `completed`), the parent is automatically moved to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`. (Covers the same state via the stage axis.)
3. Reparenting an existing item under a parent via `wl update <item> --parent <parent>` triggers the same demotion on the target parent (status `completed` or stage `in_review` → `open` / `plan_complete`).
4. No demotion occurs when the target parent is not in a completed/in_review state (e.g. `open`/`in-progress` status, or stage `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`) — behavior is otherwise unchanged.
5. The demotion is reported: JSON output includes the demoted parent (id, from status/stage, to status/stage) and human-readable output prints a summary line (e.g. `[Parent WL-XXX demoted from completed/in_review to open/plan_complete]`), following the reporting style of the priority-downgrade cascade.
6. Unit tests cover: completed parent in `in_review`, completed parent in `done`, parent in `in_review` stage, non-eligible parent (no-op), the reparenting path, and JSON/human output reporting.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The demoted state must be a valid status/stage combination per the configured compatibility table: `open` / `plan_complete` (status `open` is compatible with stage `plan_complete`; status `completed` is only compatible with `in_review`/`done`).
- Demotion applies only to the direct target parent (the parent the child is being added to). Grandparent/ancestor promotion is out of scope.
- No new config flags. The behavior is automatic, not opt-in.
- Must not interfere with existing recursive-close and recovery-close logic in `wl close`.

## Existing State

- `src/commands/create.ts` (line ~159) sets `parentId` when `--parent` is provided, with no parent lifecycle check.
- `src/commands/update.ts` (line ~198) applies `parentId` updates (reparenting) with no parent lifecycle check.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` has `cascadePriorityDowngrade(parentId, newPriority)` — the established pattern for a parent→child cascade rule, wired in `src/commands/update.ts` (~lines 384–467) with `downgradedChildren` reported in JSON and a human summary line.
- `src/commands/close.ts` implements the inverse: recursive close (deepest-first) and a recovery path for a `done` parent that still has non-closed children (children added after parent closed).

## Desired Change

1. Add a database method on `WorklogDatabase` (in `packages/shared/src/database.ts`, following the `cascadePriorityDowngrade` pattern) — e.g. `demoteParentOnChildAdded(parentId)` — that:
   - Loads the parent by id.
   - If the parent's status is `completed` (any stage) OR stage is `in_review`, updates it to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
   - Returns the demoted parent (or `null` when no demotion was needed).
2. Wire the method into `src/commands/create.ts`: after creating a child with `--parent`, call it on the parent id; include the result in JSON output and print a human summary line.
3. Wire the method into `src/commands/update.ts`: when `--parent` is provided, call it on the new parent; include the result in JSON output and print a human summary line.
4. Add unit tests in `tests/` (e.g. `tests/database.test.ts` for the method, plus command-level tests for create/update output).

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — add `demoteParentOnChildAdded(parentId)` method (canonical WorklogDatabase class; `src/database.ts` re-exports it).
- `src/commands/create.ts` — call the method after creating a child with `--parent`; report demotion in output.
- `src/commands/update.ts` — call the method when reparenting via `--parent`; report demotion in output.
- `tests/database.test.ts` (and command-level tests) — unit coverage for the method and the create/update reporting.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR — Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced**: established the cascade-rule pattern (`cascadePriorityDowngrade` on the database class, wiring + reporting in `update.ts`). This feature mirrors that pattern in the opposite direction (child addition → parent demotion).
- **WL-0MQQJDQ7M000X2L4 — wl close silently orphans children when no audit result exists**: close-side handling of the parent/child lifecycle invariant; related context for why the invariant matters.
- `src/commands/close.ts` — recursive close + recovery close for parents whose children were added after closing; this feature prevents that state from being created.
- **Automated report note (find-related WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6):** the automated run surfaced only generic keyword matches (WL-0MSA9UHH6005167Y, WL-0MP14ZDJX002KK12, WL-0MLOS7X1C1P82B5J) with no additional strongly-related items; the manual list above contains the true precedents. Full automated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6.md`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The demotion applies to both `wl create --parent` and `wl update --parent` (reparenting) — any operation that adds a child to a parent. The user's seed intent covers "when a child is added to parent"; both commands do this.
- **Assumption:** Demoted status is `open` (user answer: "1. a") — the parent is re-opened for planning.
- **Assumption:** Demotion is reported in output (user answer: "2. report"), mirroring the priority-downgrade cascade reporting style.
- **Risk:** A batch `wl update` that reparents multiple items under a completed parent will demote that parent once — harmless and idempotent (subsequent calls are no-ops).
- **Risk:** If `db.update` fails (e.g. file lock), the demotion must not crash the create/update — treat as best-effort, but surface a warning if it fails.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Only the direct parent is demoted; ancestor propagation and child-status validation elsewhere are separate concerns (tracked in existing items where applicable).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: When the parent is demoted from `completed`/`in_review` back to `plan_complete`, which status should it get? Options: a) `open`, b) `in-progress`, c) other. — Answer (user, interactive reply): "1. a" → status `open` / stage `plan_complete`. Source: interactive reply (2026-08-07).
- Q: Should the demotion be surfaced in command output (JSON + human summary line), following the priority-downgrade cascade precedent, or happen silently? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "2. report" → JSON field + human summary line. Source: interactive reply (2026-08-07).
- Note: The user's parenthetical "(sorry status should be en)" was interpreted via the clarifying question above — the demoted status is `open`.
data.title: Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added

# Intake Draft — Add per-shortcut option to control whether a shortcut opens a command pane (WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL)

## Problem statement

Every chord shortcut in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` unconditionally opens a pane when dispatched: shell commands (`!!`/`!`) open a visible "Command Output" herdr pane via `run-in-pane.sh`, and agent commands (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`) open a pi agent pane via `send-to-pi.sh`. There is no way to configure a shortcut to execute without opening a pane — high-frequency, low-feedback actions (e.g. `a-y` audit approve) force the user to dismiss a pane on every use.

## Users

- **Herdr worklist users** who drive Worklog workflows via chord shortcuts and want quiet, non-intrusive execution for actions that need no visual confirmation (approve, priority changes, etc.).
- **Producers / reviewers** using `a-y` (audit approve) repeatedly across many `in_review` items.

### User stories

- As a user, when I press a shortcut configured with `open_pane: false`, I want the command to run in the background (no pane opens) so I can keep working uninterrupted — and I want its output written to a log file so I can inspect what happened later.
- As a user, when I press any other shortcut, I want the pane to open exactly as it does today (default behavior unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Schema** — `ShortcutEntry` in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` gains an optional `openPane` boolean, parsed from the `open_pane` key in shortcuts.json. Missing/invalid values default to opening a pane (backward compatible; invalid values are logged and treated as omitted, mirroring the `code_freeze` pattern).
2. **Dispatch — shell commands** — A `!!`/`!` shortcut with `open_pane: false` executes its command in the background (no herdr pane created) with stdout/stderr captured to a log file for later inspection.
3. **Dispatch — agent commands** — An agent shortcut (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`) with `open_pane: false` runs headless (no pi agent pane created), honoring the entry's `model`, with output captured to a log file. The work-item ↔ pane association (WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9) is skipped when no pane is created.
4. **Default unchanged** — Shortcuts without `open_pane` (all current entries) behave exactly as today: shell commands open a visible command-output pane; agent commands open a pi agent pane.
5. **Test case applied** — The `a-y` (audit approve) entry in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` is set to `open_pane: false`; pressing `a-y` approves the item without opening a pane, and the worklist refresh shows the updated state.
6. **All related documentation is updated** — `packages/herdr/README.md` (shortcut schema section, alongside `model` and `code_freeze`) documents the new `open_pane` field and its semantics.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes, including new unit tests for parsing/validation and dispatch routing (shell + agent, pane vs. no-pane, log-file creation).

## Constraints

- Follow the established optional-field pattern in `shortcut-config.ts` (`model`, `code_freeze`): snake_case JSON key → camelCase TS field, invalid values never break or hide a shortcut.
- Background execution must be detached and non-blocking — the TUI event loop and process lifecycle must be unaffected (mirror the existing `spawn(..., { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' })` + `child.unref()` pattern in `index.ts`).
- No behavior change for entries without `open_pane` (default = open pane).
- Log file location is an implementation decision; a sensible default is a per-run file under a known directory (e.g. the OS tmpdir or `<worklog-root>`), with the path recorded/logged so it can be located for inspection.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — 22 entries; `a-y` is `["a","y"]` → `!!wl reviewed <id> false && wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close yes --summary 'Approved by manual review'` (view `both`, stages `in_review`).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `ShortcutEntry` interface (command, view, chord, label?, description?, stages?, model?, codeFreeze?) + `parseShortcutEntry` validation + `ShortcutRegistry`; optional fields follow snake_case→camelCase parsing with invalid-value logging.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `onCommand(command, model)` routes: `agent` → `send-to-pi.sh` (pi pane, claims item, optional pane-id capture); `pane` (`!!`/`!`) → `run-in-pane.sh` (visible Command Output pane); `stdout` → `CMD:` prefix fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `processChordInput` resolves chords and stores `resolvedCommand` / `resolvedModel` on `ChordState`; `resolveAndRouteCommand` calls `onCommand(resolvedCommand, model)`.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — splits a pane right, runs the command in a shell wrapper, keeps the pane open for inspection.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — opens a pi agent pane with the command as initial prompt; `--model` / `--pane-id-file` options exist.
- Headless pi execution (`pi -p --mode json`) is an established pattern elsewhere (e.g. `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`).

## Desired change

- Add `open_pane: false` support to the shortcut schema, plumbed through `parseShortcutEntry` → `ChordState` → `onCommand`, defaulting to open-pane behavior.
- In `index.ts` dispatch: when a shortcut entry has `openPane: false`, spawn the shell command (or headless pi for agent commands) detached with output redirected to a log file instead of opening a pane; skip pane-id capture for agent commands; keep the worklist refresh cycle so results become visible.
- Set `a-y` to `open_pane: false` in `shortcuts.json` as the proof/test case.
- Document the field in `packages/herdr/README.md`; add unit tests for parsing and dispatch.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — Add `openPane?: boolean` to `ShortcutEntry`; parse/validate `open_pane` in `parseShortcutEntry` (default true, invalid → logged + omitted).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Set `"open_pane": false` on the `a-y` (audit approve) entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Plumb resolved `openPane` through `ChordState` (`resolvedOpenPane`) and `onCommand` signature (`command, model, openPane`).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Branch dispatch on `openPane`: background execution with log-file redirect (shell: `bash -c` detached; agent: headless `pi -p --mode json` honoring `model`) vs. current pane-opening paths; skip pane-id capture when no pane opens.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — Parsing tests: `open_pane: true/false/omitted/invalid`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (or worklist tests) — Dispatch routing tests: no-pane shell + agent, log file written, default still opens panes.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Document the `open_pane` field alongside `model` / `code_freeze` (schema table + behavior notes).

## Related work

- WL-0MS95CEAE0080EB4 — *a-y (audit approve) shortcut does nothing — should run wl command visibly in a herdr pane* (completed): introduced the visible-pane execution for `!!` commands that this feature now makes optional.
