# Intake brief: Herdr — flipping `needsProducerReview` must not make a valid audit stale

**Work item:** WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R (bug, medium)

## Problem statement

Flipping the `needsProducerReview` flag (e.g. `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review true`, as the heartbeat does when flagging an item for producer review) bumps the work item's `updatedAt`. herdr's audit-freshness predicate `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` then reports the previously valid audit as **stale**, which (a) degrades the TUI audit icon from the passed glyph to the stale-passed/stage glyph, and (b) makes the downtime audit tier re-select the item for a wasteful `/skill:audit` re-run of unchanged content. A review-state flag is metadata, not content — it must not invalidate an audit.

## Users

- **Producer** — flips `needsProducerReview` (via TUI flag toggle or `wl update --needs-producer-review`) to signal review intent. Should see the item's existing green "audit passed" state unchanged.
  - User story: "As a producer, when I flag an item for review, I want its audit result to remain visibly passed, so I can trust that only genuinely changed items need re-auditing."
- **Herdr downtime worker** — dispatches `/skill:audit` for items without a valid audit during idle time. Should not burn an audit run on items whose only change since the audit was a review flag.
  - User story: "As the audit-tier dispatcher, I want to skip items whose audit is stale only because of a metadata flag flip, so idle time is spent auditing items whose content actually changed."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `WorklogDatabase.update()` persists a `needsProducerReview`-only change but **preserves** `updatedAt` (no bump). A change to any content field (title, description, status, stage, priority, sortIndex, parentId, tags, assignee, issueType, risk, effort) still bumps `updatedAt` exactly as today.
- [ ] Unit test (packages/shared): `update()` with only `needsProducerReview` flipped → flag persisted, `updatedAt` unchanged.
- [ ] Unit test (packages/shared): `update()` with a content field + flag in the same call → `updatedAt` bumped (combined update still bumps).
- [ ] Regression (packages/shared): no-op update and content-only update behave exactly as today (no-op preserves, content bumps).
- [ ] Herdr integration verification: after a flag-only update, `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` remains **true** for a previously fresh audit → TUI shows the passed icon (not the stale glyph) and `selectAuditCandidate` does **not** select the item (no redundant `/skill:audit` dispatch). Herdr code itself is unchanged (single source of truth stays in worklog).
- [ ] Documentation: comment on `update()`/the `fieldsToCompare` split documents why `needsProducerReview` is excluded from the timestamp-bump trigger; the `isAuditFresh` doc comment in `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` notes the guarantee ("flag-only flips do not move `updatedAt`").
- [ ] All related documentation updated (code comments, README/docs as applicable).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the **worklog core** (`packages/shared/src/database.ts` `update()`), per operator decision — not in herdr. herdr's `isAuditFresh` and `selectAuditCandidate` stay untouched; they automatically benefit once `updatedAt` stops moving on flag flips.
- Do not change the meaning of `updatedAt` for content changes: sync field-conflict resolution ("newer `updatedAt` wins", `src/sync.ts`) and `wl recent` ordering rely on it. Accepted caveat (operator-approved): a flag-only flip no longer bumps `updatedAt`, so a concurrent remote content edit could out-rank the flag in a field-conflict merge (low severity — the flag is a review signal, not content).
- The no-op fast path (`hasChanged` false → preserve `updatedAt`, no store write) must remain; the flag-only path must still **write** the flag while preserving the timestamp (it must not take the early return).
- `needsProducerReview` is the only field moved to the no-bump set; no other fields change semantics (minimal, surgical).
- Out of scope: the audit skill's own pipeline freshness (already handled by the content-fingerprint gate, SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT — a flag flip doesn't change the fingerprint); WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE (at-or-near freshness for the audit's own persistence write) is a separate item.

## Existing state

1. `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `update()`: `fieldsToCompare` includes `needsProducerReview`; if any tracked field changed → `updated.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()`.
2. `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)`: `auditTime > updateTime - 60000` (60 s buffer). A post-audit `updatedAt` bump → not fresh → stale.
3. `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` `getIconPrefix()` (line ~367): for `in_review`, `fresh ? auditIcon(...) : (auditResult === true ? auditStaleIcon(...) : stageIcon(...))` — the stale glyph path.
4. `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `selectAuditCandidate()` (line ~1043): filters `!isAuditFresh(c.auditedAt, c.updatedAt)` → stale item becomes an audit-dispatch candidate (subject to 7-day recency window and dispatched-marker exclusion).
5. `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `getNextAuditCandidate()` (line ~371): audit tier pulls candidates from `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` and routes through `selectAuditCandidate`.
6. Heartbeat (`skill/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py`) flags the next ready item via `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review true` — the trigger of the reported symptom.

## Desired change

In `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `update()`, split the change detection:

- `contentFieldsToCompare` = current `fieldsToCompare` **minus** `needsProducerReview` — any change here bumps `updatedAt` (unchanged behavior).
- `needsProducerReview` is a **metadata** field: a flag-only change persists the flag but preserves `updatedAt` (does not take the no-op early return, and does not bump the timestamp).
- Combined content+flag change → bump (as today).
- herdr: **no code change**; add/refresh a doc comment on `isAuditFresh` stating the guarantee and re-verify the icon + dispatch behavior via tests in `packages/herdr`.

## Key Files:

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `WorklogDatabase.update()`; split `fieldsToCompare` into content (bump) vs metadata (`needsProducerReview`, preserve `updatedAt`); keep the no-op fast path distinct from the flag-only path
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` (or existing shared test location) — new unit tests: flag-only (persist, preserve), content+flag (bump), no-op, content-only (unchanged behavior)
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — doc comment on `isAuditFresh` (guarantee: flag-only flips do not move `updatedAt`); no logic change
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — no change; referenced for verification that `selectAuditCandidate` stops selecting flag-staled items
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.test.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — integration-style regression checks (fresh audit after flag-only update → passed icon, not a dispatch candidate)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Sync conflict (accepted, low):** `src/sync.ts` field-conflict resolution picks the newer `updatedAt`; a flag-only flip no longer bumps it, so a concurrent remote content edit could out-rank the flag in a conflict merge. Mitigation: the flag is a review signal, not content — re-flagging is cheap and the next sync merge reconciles. Operator-approved in Q1.
- **`wl recent` ordering:** `src/commands/recent.ts` sorts by `updatedAt`; flag flips will no longer surface items as "recently updated". Arguably more correct (a review flag is not activity); document in the change notes.
- **Herdr dispatch recency window:** a flag-only flip no longer extends the 7-day audit-recency window (`DOWNTIME_AUDIT_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS`) — an old item flagged for review stays outside the window, unchanged from today (recency is about content activity, not review intent).
- **Scope-creep guard:** WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE (at-or-near freshness for the audit's own persistence write) is a separate item — do not fold it in here. The alternative "content-version signal" approach (Q1 option B) is explicitly out of scope.
- **Assumption:** herdr is the only timestamp-freshness consumer that matters for this bug; `heartbeat.py` checks `wl audit-show` rawOutput ("Ready to close: Yes"), not freshness, so it is unaffected either way.

## Related work

- WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE (open, bug, medium) — "Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher": *opposite direction* (audit's own persistence write must not look stale). Shares the same `isAuditFresh` predicate; complement, not duplicate. Coordinate so the two fixes don't conflict on the predicate.
- WL-0MS1OJZL7005CR7A (completed) — "Show distinct icon when audit is stale but readyToClose is true": introduced the stale-passed icon behavior.
- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG (completed) — "Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit": the audit-tier dispatch feature.
- WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (completed) — "Audit candidate selection".
- SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT (SorraAgents) — content-fingerprint freshness gate in the audit runner; the pipeline-side precedent for "non-content updates must not invalidate an audit".
- WL-0MLGTWT4S1X4HDD9 / WL-0MLQ0ZHQE0JBX8Y6 (completed) — `--needs-producer-review` filter and TUI shortcut; the flag feature this fix interacts with.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should the fix live? (A) Worklog core — `wl update` persists a `needsProducerReview`-only change but preserves `updatedAt` (flag is metadata, not content), fixing herdr display + dispatch with one change; caveat: sync field-conflict resolution could drop a flag flip racing a concurrent remote content edit. (B) Herdr-side only — requires worklog to emit a new content-version signal (bigger). (C) Both / other." — Answer (user): **A — Worklog core**. Source: interactive reply. Research: `WorklogDatabase.update()` (packages/shared/src/database.ts) is the single write path for `wl update`; herdr's `isAuditFresh`/`selectAuditCandidate` consume only timestamps, so preserving `updatedAt` on flag-only writes fixes both consumers without herdr changes.
- Q2: "Scope — the stale audit shows up in herdr as (1) TUI icon degradation and (2) re-dispatch of `/skill:audit`. Cover both (shared predicate), or only dispatch?" — Answer (user): **Both**. Source: interactive reply. Research: both effects derive from the same `isAuditFresh` predicate (icons.ts:250, used at icons.ts:367 and downtime-worker.ts:1043); fixing the root cause (no `updatedAt` bump) resolves both; herdr-side regression tests verify both paths.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQ3LYSPS006V60H** – TUI does not auto-refresh after CLI audit update (completed)
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** – Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon (completed)
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** – Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the selection list (open)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — audit/auditedAt/isAuditFresh/freshness/updatedAt/stale semantics documented in the herdr package README

# Compress the space used in herdr plugin meta-data

## Problem Statement

The metadata section in the herdr plugin's list-mode metadata panel and detail view
occupies too much vertical space. Key related fields are displayed on separate rows
when they could be compacted, wasting limited terminal real estate.

## Users

- **Terminal users viewing work items** — want to see more metadata at a glance without
  scrolling through verbose, line-by-line display.
- **Users with limited terminal height** — benefit from denser metadata presentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Status + Stage** are displayed on the same row, e.g. `Status+Stage: 🔄 in_progress / 🛠️ in_progress` (or similar compact format).
2. **Priority + Type** are displayed on the same row, e.g. `Priority+Type: ⭐ high / feature`.
3. **Created + Updated** are displayed on the same row, e.g. `Created+Updated: 01/08/26 10:00 / 02/08/26 10:00`.
4. **Audit + Audited At** are displayed on the same row, e.g. `Audit+AuditedAt: ✅ ready to close / 03/08/26 10:00`.
5. The detail view metadata table is also compressed consistently (the same field pairings).
6. All other metadata rows (ID, Title, Risk, Effort, Children, Parent, Tags, GitHub Issue, Reviewed) remain unchanged.
7. Full project test suite passes with changes.

## Constraints

- Existing field labels and icon behavior must be preserved (no changes to icon mapping).
- The compact format should be readable — avoid over-compression that harms scannability.
- No changes to the `WorkItem` type or data model — purely a display change.
- `noIcons` mode (plain text) must also be handled correctly for compacted rows.

## Existing State

- `buildMetaRows()` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` returns an array of `[label, value]` pairs, one per row.
- `formatMetadataPanel()` renders each pair as a separate line: `  <label padded> <value>`.
- `formatDetailContent()` similarly renders the detail view table.
- Key files:
  - `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `buildMetaRows()`, `formatMetadataPanel()`, `formatDetailContent()`
  - `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — tests for metadata row building and formatting

## Desired Change

Introduce paired-row rendering for the four specified field pairs. Options considered:

1. **Change `buildMetaRows` to emit compound rows** — modify the data structure to return
   pairs-of-pairs for the four groupings, then update rendering.
2. **Keep `buildMetaRows` unchanged, introduce a post-processing step** — leave the row
   data intact but compress during rendering in `formatMetadataPanel` and `formatDetailContent`.

**Recommendation:** Option 2 — less invasive, keeps `buildMetaRows` as the single source
of truth for field data, and localizes the rendering logic change.

## Related Work

- WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9 — Icon + text metadata values (ensures icon handling is consistent).
- WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J — Dynamic metadata panel sizing.
- WL-0MSEPP0MB009K9PR — Responsive metadata panel layout implementation.
- WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7 — Herdr metadata panel: drop duplicate ID row from data section.

## Summary

`npm run build` in `packages/herdr` exits 2 with 84 `TS6059` errors (`File ... is not under 'rootDir' '/home/.../packages/herdr/src'`).

## Root cause

`packages/herdr/tsconfig.json` sets `rootDir: ./src` and includes `src/**/*.ts`, which includes the `.test.ts` files. Several herdr test files (e.g. `src/implement-tier-blocked-exclusion.test.ts`, worklist tests) import shared CLI test helpers from the repo root (`../../tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`, `../../src/*`). Those files are pulled into the compilation graph but lie outside `rootDir`, producing TS6059 for every import. tsc still emits the in-root files to `dist/`, but the `cp src/shortcuts.json dist/shortcuts.json` step of the build script never runs (tsc exits non-zero), leaving `dist/shortcuts.json` stale.

## Expected behaviour

- `cd packages/herdr && npm run build` exits 0 and copies `src/shortcuts.json` → `dist/shortcuts.json`.

## Implementation notes

- Exclude test files from the herdr build: add `"exclude": ["**/*.test.ts"]` to `packages/herdr/tsconfig.json` (the test files are compiled/run by vitest, not needed in dist). Verify `npm run build` exits 0 and `dist/` contains no `.test.js` files.
- Check whether `packages/shared/tsconfig.json` has the same pattern (it builds cleanly today — likely no test files there).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cd packages/herdr && npm run build` exits 0.
- [ ] `dist/shortcuts.json` is copied on every build.
- [ ] `npx vitest run packages/herdr` still passes (tests unaffected by the exclude).

Discovered from: WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4

# Intake Brief: Herdr hydrator — rescue in_progress work items with no active pane

## Headline

Add a hydration task to the herdr worklist plugin that, every 30 seconds, fetches all `in_progress` work items, matches each against the work-item IDs embedded in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace (via the pane-title work WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), and demotes any item with no matching pane out of `in_progress` to `completed` (stage `in_review`), `blocked` (dependency-blocked), or `open` (otherwise). The check also runs immediately when the tab regains focus.

## Problem statement

Work items are sometimes left stuck in `status=in_progress` even though no agent pane is actually working on them (e.g. the agent pane was closed, the session died, or the item was claimed and abandoned). There is currently no automatic mechanism to detect this, so stale in-progress items linger at the top of work queues and are never re-selected.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want a self-healing work queue where an item only stays `in_progress` while an active agent pane is genuinely attached to it.
  - As a producer, I want items whose agent pane has died to be demoted automatically so they re-enter the selection pool instead of rotting in `in_progress`.
- **Herdr worklist users** — benefit from a queue that reflects reality without manual cleanup.
  - As a user, I want the worklist to keep `in_progress` items only when a matching pane exists, so the list stays honest.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every 30 seconds the hydrator fetches all `in_progress` work items (`wl list --status in_progress`).
2. For each item, the hydrator attempts to match an **active pane**: a pane, in **any tab of the current workspace**, whose pane title contains the work item's ID (`WL-…`) and that is still running (present in `herdr pane list`). Matching relies on the pane-title format introduced by the blocking work item (e.g. `Manually triggered implement <title> - WL-<id>`).
3. Any `in_progress` item with **no matching active pane** is demoted:
   - stage `in_review` → `status=completed`
   - item has an active outbound dependency blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`) → `status=blocked`
   - otherwise → `status=open`
   Transitions respect the project's status/stage compatibility rules (e.g. `blocked` only allows stages `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`, so a stage `in_progress` item demoted to `blocked` must also have its stage demoted).
4. When the worklist tab regains focus, the hydration check runs **immediately** (not waiting for the next 30s tick), reusing the existing visibility resume-poll mechanism.
5. The hydrator is **safe**: no transition is made for an item whose matching pane is found; the task is single-flight; failures (CLI missing, unparseable output) are logged and never crash the plugin; no `wl` spawns happen while the worklist pane is hidden.
6. Unit tests cover: pane-title ID extraction, active-pane matching across tabs, each demotion decision (in_review→completed, dependency-blocked→blocked, else→open), stage/status compatibility handling, focus-resume immediate run, and fail-open error paths.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked on WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** ("Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned") — the hydrator matches panes by the work-item ID embedded in pane titles; it must not be implemented before that title format lands. (The in-progress duplicate WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D carries the same work; block on the intake-complete one.)
- The 30s loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker) — acceptable per the operator; the focus-resume immediate check is required.
- "Active pane" = any running pane whose title contains the work-item ID, across **all tabs** in the current workspace; focus/zoom state does not matter (matching is by title presence + pane existence, not focus).
- Reuse the existing `TaskScheduler` (packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts) and the visibility `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery in `worklist.ts`; do not add a second interval loop.
- Fail-open at every boundary: never crash the plugin, never demote on ambiguous evidence (missing pane list, unparseable output → treat as "no match" only when the CLI output is actually trustworthy).
- No schema changes; pure status/stage updates via the `wl` CLI.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the worklist TUI registers a single `TaskScheduler` with tasks: `refresh` (auto-refresh), `sync`, `resume-poll` (hidden→visible immediate refresh), and `downtime` (downtime-worker tick, 30s default). The hydrator would be a sibling task.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — `TaskScheduler` with 1s base tick, per-task `intervalMs`, `singleFlight`, and `runTimeoutMs` watchdog; a rejecting task never takes down the loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — `isPaneVisible()` + `PollGate` (TTL memoizer); tab focus via `herdr tab get <id>` is the visibility signal; resume-poll uses it to detect hidden→visible.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — existing work-item ↔ pane association file (`.worklog/agent-panes.json`) and `herdr agent list` parsing; a possible secondary signal but the hydrator matches by pane-title per the operator's decision.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `runWl(...)`, `extractJson`, `extractItems` helpers for wl CLI JSON.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/toggle.sh` — precedent for `herdr pane list` JSON parsing (panes with `label`/`pane_id` across the workspace).
- `src/commands/dep.ts` — `wl dep list <id>` returns `outbound` edges with target `id`/`status`/`priority`; `packages/shared/src/database.ts:isDependencyActive` defines an active blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`).
- `src/config.ts` — status/stage compatibility: `in-progress` allows `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`; `blocked` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`; `completed` allows `in_review`/`done`; `open` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`.

## Desired change

1. Add a hydrator module (e.g. `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`):
   - `extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes)` — parse `WL-[0-9A-Z]+` from pane titles.
   - `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes)` — item ID present in any running pane title across all tabs.
   - `decideDemotion(item)` — pure decision: `in_review` → `completed`; dependency-blocked → `blocked`; else → `open` (with stage/status compatibility handling).
   - `runHydrationOnce(deps)` — fetch `wl list --status in_progress`, fetch `herdr pane list`, match, apply demotions via `wl update`.
2. Register the hydrator in `worklist.ts` as a scheduler task (`id: 'hydrate'`, `intervalMs: 30_000`, `singleFlight: true`, `runTimeoutMs` set) that is visibility-gated (skip while hidden, zero wl spawns when hidden).
3. Hook the hidden→visible transition: when the resume-poll detects visibility, run the hydration check immediately in addition to the existing refresh.
4. Add unit tests (see AC6) mirroring the existing downtime-worker test harness (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, injectable exec seam from `fetcher.ts`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — new module: ID extraction, pane matching, demotion decision, orchestration (the bulk of the work).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — register the `hydrate` scheduler task; trigger immediate check on focus-resume.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — reused as-is (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — reused `runWl`/`extractJson`/`extractItems` helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — reused `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — new test suite (AC6).
- `src/config.ts` — reference only: status/stage compatibility rules that constrain demotion.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — reference only: dependency-blocked semantics (`isDependencyActive`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** — "Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned" (open, intake_complete) — **BLOCKING**: introduces the pane-title format containing the work-item ID that the hydrator matches on. In-progress duplicate: **WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D** (same title).
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** — "Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon" (in_review) — pane↔work-item association machinery; `agent-panes.json` is a candidate secondary signal.
- **WL-0MS9NPHQU005Y3VE** — "Herdr plugin should set work-item status to in_progress when instigating actions" (completed) — the counter-direction: sets `in_progress` on dispatch; the hydrator demotes when no pane remains.
- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime" (completed) — downtime worker: the 30s scheduler-task precedent the hydrator mirrors.
- **WL-0MSJNJPRM009RM35** — "Gate worklist auto-refresh on tab focus so a visible pane in a multi-pane tab keeps refreshing" (in_progress) — visibility-gating precedent reused by the hydrator.
- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — "Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible" (completed) — related zero-spawn-when-hidden concern.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** pane titles will contain the work-item ID once WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y lands — the hydrator is blocked on that and must not guess other signals.
- **Risk:** demoting an item the operator considers genuinely in-progress (pane title missing/renamed by hand, pane in a different workspace). Mitigation: matching is by title + pane existence across all tabs; the 30s cadence + focus-resume means demotions are re-visible quickly; keep the demotion decision pure and well-tested.
- **Risk:** status/stage compatibility rejects a demotion (e.g. `blocked` with stage `in_progress`). Mitigation: `decideDemotion` returns a compatible (status, stage) pair; transitions that fail validation are logged, not retried blindly.
- **Risk:** `herdr pane list` output shape differs (tabs vs panes). Mitigation: fail-open parsing like toggle.sh/agent-tracker; treat unparseable output as "no demotion this cycle".
- **Risk:** scope creep (agent-panes.json matching, notifications, configurable intervals). Mitigation: record as linked work items; this intake covers pane-title matching only.
- **Scope-creep guard:** secondary signals (agent-panes.json, `herdr agent list` states) are explicitly out of scope for the initial implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When no active pane matches an in_progress item, HOW should the hydrator choose between completed / blocked / open? (a) Signal-based: stage in_review → completed; blocked-by dependencies → blocked; otherwise → open; (b) always open; (c) operator picks per item; (d) other" — Answer (user): **a** — signal-based. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "The herdr plugin's 30s scheduler loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker). That means the hydrator only runs while a worklist pane is open. Acceptable, or should it run standalone?" — Answer (user): **acceptable**, ensure the check runs immediately when the tab gets focus. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Does 'active pane' mean any pane whose title contains the work-item ID and is still running (regardless of focus/zoom), across all tabs in the current workspace?" — Answer (user): **yes**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1** – wl next should return parent items instead of surfacing children individually (completed)
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** – Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon (completed)
- **WL-0MSC0O8HN000EBFH** – Herdr plugin: free-form prompt shortcut opens new pi pane (option B) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-Herdr-hydrator-rescue-in-progress-work-items-with-no-active-pane-WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI.md` — matched: 000, 0ms9nphqu005y3ve, 0msb1n0hb0007n6n, 0msbqujqx005rat9, 0msf49fmw009m06k (+409 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSOKOI4J0046GE5-remove-stray-compiled-artifacts-committe/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 000, 0msb1n0hb0007n6n, 0msf49fmw009m06k, 0msjnjprm009rm35, 30s (+272 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 000, 0msb1n0hb0007n6n, 0msf49fmw009m06k, 0msjnjprm009rm35, 30s (+272 more)

# Feature Request: tolerant work-item ID resolution in `wl show` for agent tool use

## Problem statement

The SorraAgents audit skill ships `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py find-workitem <id>`,
which resolves a work item by shelling out to `wl search <id> --json` and then
post-filtering the results for an exact id match. Agents are directed to this
wrapper because the native wl CLI has no single command that tolerantly
resolves a work-item ID:

- `wl show <id>` is exact-match only (`db.get(normalizedId)`); a partial,
  case-differing, or truncated ID fails with "Work item not found".
- `wl list <term>` performs case-insensitive **substring** matching over
  id/title/description — this is the optimal substring-search primitive — but
  returns a list of matches, not a single resolved item.
- `wl search <query>` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) — it is
  NOT a substring matcher.

So there is a gap: no single native command does "given an ID reference,
resolve the item" with tolerant (exact-first, unique-substring-fallback)
matching. This feature closes that gap so agent tooling (and humans) can use
one native command instead of a wrapper.

## User story

As an agent (or user) holding an ID reference that may be exact, truncated, or
partial, I want `wl show` to resolve it tolerantly — exact match first, then a
unique case-insensitive substring match on the id — with a clear structured
error when the reference is ambiguous — so I can resolve a work item with a
single native `wl show` call.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl show <id> --json` returns the work item when `<id>` matches an item id
   exactly (current behavior preserved, including `normalizeCliId` case/prefix
   normalization).
2. When no exact id matches but exactly one work item's **id** contains `<id>`
   case-insensitively as a substring, `wl show` resolves to that item and
   returns `success: true` with the item (JSON mode), with no error.
3. When multiple items match (ambiguous), `wl show` exits non-zero with a
   structured error `ambiguous-match` listing the candidate ids in JSON mode,
   and a human-readable disambiguation hint otherwise.
4. When nothing matches, `wl show` keeps the existing "Work item not found"
   behavior (non-zero exit, structured error in JSON mode).
5. `--json` output remains machine-parseable in all three outcome paths
   (found / ambiguous / not found).
6. New vitest coverage for: exact match, unique substring match, ambiguous
   match, and not-found — in both JSON and human output modes.
7. Documentation updated (CLI.md / EXAMPLES.md / docs command reference) to
   describe the tolerant resolution and the `ambiguous-match` error.

## Design notes (suggested, not prescriptive)

- Resolution order: exact id (via `normalizeCliId`) → unique case-insensitive
  substring match over item ids → ambiguity/not-found handling. Keep the
  fallback scoped to the **id** field (not title/description) to minimise
  surprise ambiguity; `wl list <term>` remains the canonical way to search
  title/description substrings.
- Reuse the existing `db.list()` substring filter logic from `list.ts` for the
  fallback so behaviour stays consistent.
- Consider a `--exact` flag to force strict exact-match behaviour for callers
  that need it.

## Out of scope

- No change to `wl list <term>` substring semantics (already canonical).
- No change to `wl search` (FTS) behaviour or index.
- No semantic/embedding matching.

## Related

- Unblocks: SorraAgents work item "Replace scan.py find-workitem with native
  wl CLI lookup in audit prompts" (tracked in the SorraAgents worklog; this
  item is its blocker).
- Context: SorraAgents SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI refined audit prompt guidance to
  `wl list <term> --json` (substring) + `scan.py find-workitem <id>` (exact,
  interim) for worklog lookups; scan.py find-workitem is the wrapper this
  feature replaces.
data.title: Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to wl show (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool use

# Lower downtime worker idle threshold + poll interval

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime worker (`createDowntimeWorker` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) only dispatches local-LLM work after the local model has been **continuously idle for the full idle threshold**, default `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 240_000` (4 min), polled every `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000` (30s). Analysis of llama-proxy logs (2026-08-11 overnight, 01:00-11:57) shows the local model busy only 43.6% of the time, with long stretches of partial idle (03:00-10:00 avg 0.87-1.33 slots busy of 2). Every idle gap shorter than 4 minutes is currently skipped — those gaps are missed local-dispatch opportunities that instead go to remote providers.

Goal: maximize local LLM utilization by dispatching into shorter idle gaps.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` lowered from 240_000 to 60_000 (60s), with the `clampDowntimeIdleThresholdMs` floor (1s) unchanged.
2. `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` lowered from 30_000 to 10_000 (the existing `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS` floor), so idle onset is detected faster.
3. Existing test suite updated: clamps still enforce floors (10s poll floor, 1s threshold floor); idle-threshold timing tests use the new default; no test asserts the old 240s/30s values.
4. Settings persistence unchanged (defaults flow through `defaultSettings`); deployed `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` is untouched (only `browseItemCount` set today — defaults apply).
5. Full project test suite passes (quiet mode).

## Notes

- A race (dispatch fires as an interactive request arrives) is acceptable: the agent request simply falls back to remote, same as today — worst case is no worse than the status quo.
- The audit tier's subprocess fan-out and the all-slots-free gate are UNCHANGED by this item (see the separate per-slot-identity / tier-aware dispatch work for that).
- Related: LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 (per-slot identity) would let a future `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots: N` dispatch into partial-idle states; this item only tightens timing, not the slot gate.
data.title: Lower downtimeIdleThresholdMs 240s -> ~60s (plus downtimePollIntervalMs 30s -> 10s floor)

# Intake Brief: Sync — Regression Guard

## Problem Statement

When `wl sync` merges remote state that is newer than local, it can silently import regressions: fields the local store had set to non-default values (e.g. `effort: 'Small'`, `status: completed`) get overwritten with defaults by a stale/divergent second store, as observed Aug 6–10, 2026 on the llm worklog ref.

## Users

- **Primary**: Operators of multi-store worklog setups — anyone running more than one `wl sync` instance against the same remote.
- **Secondary**: Producers/reviewers whose audit results (status/stage transitions) are silently reverted by stale syncs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During merge, for each incoming remote item with a newer `updatedAt` than local, detect regressions where a field moves from a non-default value to its default on the fields that participate in the merge: `status`/`stage` (non-default → default, e.g. `completed/in_review` → `open/idea`), `priority` (non-default → default), and `assignee` (set → unset).

   **`effort`/`risk` (producer resolution, 2026-08-23): stay PERMANENTLY EXCLUDED from the merge field lists** — ping-pong prevention by construction. A remote `effort: ''` / `risk: ''` never enters the merge; local non-default values are always kept. The guard additionally REPORTS any attempted effort/risk regression (remote non-empty → default) as a protected conflict (local kept, nothing imported) for observability, but no override path is needed for these two fields since they cannot be imported through the merge.
2. On detecting a regression, `wl sync` refuses to import that item's regressed fields: reports the conflict (item id, field, old local value, new remote default value) and keeps the local value. An explicit override flag (`--accept-regressions` or equivalent) allows the operator to accept the regression.
3. Genuine concurrent edits (both stores changed different non-default fields, or both changed the same field to different non-default values) still merge and re-timestamp exactly as today — this guard must NOT change legitimate conflict resolution.
4. The regression guard applies only to the `import()`/merge path used by `wl sync` — it does NOT affect explicit user `wl update` commands, which remain authoritative.
5. Unit tests cover: (a) newer remote with `effort: ''` against local `effort: 'Small'` → local kept (exclusion by construction), conflict REPORTED as protected, remote value NOT imported; (b) newer remote with `status: open` against local `completed` → refused, local kept, conflict reported; (c) both sides non-default differing → normal merge + re-timestamp (no regression path — guard must NOT alter legitimate conflict resolution); (d) override flag accepts the regression for merge-participating fields only; (e) `--dry-run` reports the same refusals.
6. Manual verification: sync against the known commit `5fc880a` (effort/risk cleared) → regressions refused and reported; sync against `54b1375` (restored values) → no regression flags.

## Constraints

- Must not change behavior for legitimate concurrent edits — the guard is regression-only, not conflict-resolution.
- Must be deterministic: dry-run and normal sync report the same refusals.
- Does NOT prevent a second store from pushing — it prevents the primary store from absorbing regressive state.
- Complements the identity gate (WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB) — the identity gate catches the writer; this guard catches the damage even if the writer's identity is unknown.

## Existing State

The merge functions (`mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` in `src/sync.ts`) already implement a non-default-preference heuristic: when one side has a non-default value and the other has a default, the non-default is preserved. The `isDefaultValue` helper in `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` classifies empty strings, `undefined`, and empty arrays as defaults.

The merge field arrays include `status`, `stage`, `priority`, and `assignee` — these fields **already** keep the local non-default value when the remote sends a default (via the `!localIsDefault && remoteIsDefault` branch). They do **not** produce an explicit regression report — the local value is silently kept.

The merge field arrays do **not** include `effort` or `risk` — these fields are never merged at all; the local value is always preserved regardless of the remote.

**Contradiction — RESOLVED (producer decision, 2026-08-23)**: The 13-field merge list currently excludes `effort`/`risk` (code-confirmed), yet the original ACs listed them as regression targets. Producer directive: *"The goal is to prevent ping-pong — do what you need to."* Resolution: **Reading A** — `effort`/`risk` remain excluded from the merge lists; adding them to the merge would re-introduce the ping-pong (the DB re-timestamp amplifier in `hasWorkItemChanged` already tracks these fields, so a single unguarded import becomes the newest record and propagates). The guard therefore targets the merge-participating fields (`status`/`stage`/`priority`/`assignee`), and `effort`/`risk` regressions are reported as protected (local kept). Effort/risk merge-participation is a non-goal.

## Desired Change

Add a regression detection layer on top of the merge path that:
- Identifies fields regressing from non-default → default in newer remote state, for the merge-participating fields: `status`/`stage`/`priority`/`assignee`
- Reports conflicts with details (item id, field, old value, new value)
- Refuses to import regressed fields (keeping local) unless overridden (`--accept-regressions`, merge-participating fields only)
- Preserves all existing merge behavior for non-regression cases
- Reports (without importing) attempted `effort`/`risk` regressions as protected — these fields remain excluded from the merge lists (non-goal: adding them back)

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Regression detection logic breaks existing merge behavior | High | Unit tests must verify non-regression cases still merge correctly (AC3) |
| Scope creep: "regression" definition might be too broad (e.g., should a valid transition like `in_progress → open` count as regression?) | Medium | Strict definition: only non-default → default transitions count |
| Override flag (`--accept-regressions`) could be misused, allowing silent data loss | Medium | Require explicit flag; report what was accepted in output |
| **DECIDED**: effort/risk must NOT be added to the merge list | — | Producer resolution 2026-08-23: adding them re-introduces ping-pong (DB re-timestamp amplifier `hasWorkItemChanged` tracks these fields; one unguarded import becomes the newest record) |
| `isDefaultValue` may not correctly identify defaults for all fields (e.g., custom stages) | Low | Only built-in defaults (`open`, `idea`, `medium`, empty strings) are guarded; custom stages fall through to normal merge |
| **Scope-creep risk**: The guard could be extended to "merge strategies" or general conflict-policy work — those are separate concerns. | Medium | Record as future work items; do not implement here |

**Assumptions**:
- The `isDefaultValue` function correctly classifies all default values for the fields in question
- Regression detection can be cleanly layered on top of existing merge logic without restructuring
- The operator will accept a new CLI flag for override

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/sync.ts` — `mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`: add regression detection alongside the existing merge logic (field lists UNCHANGED for `effort`/`risk` — exclusion is the ping-pong prevention)
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — `isDefaultValue`: may need no changes (already classifies empties as defaults)
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — CLI flag for `--accept-regressions`, conflict reporting in output
- `tests/sync-regression-guard.test.ts` — new test file for regression detection scenarios

## Related Work

| ID | Title | Relationship |
|----|-------|-------------|
| WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB | Sync: identity gate — refuse merge of foreign/empty-author commits | Related: same root cause incident (Aug 2026 llm worklog pollution); identity gate catches the writer, regression guard catches the damage |
| WL-0MSORD6HC005QVZX | Sync: do not change updatedAt on whitespace-only changes | Completed; orthogonal concern |
| WL-0MKVZ510K1XHJ7B3 | Sync & data integrity | Completed; foundational sync merge logic |
| WL-0MSUEOAQO0081TJH | Wire identity gate into wl sync + config flag + sync-point persistence | Completed; identity gate now wired into sync |

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- **Q (auto-resolved by code inspection)**: The description says "the 13-field merge list currently excludes effort/risk" — the code confirms `effort` and `risk` are NOT in the merge field arrays. Does this mean: (a) the ACs about effort/risk are stale and should be removed, or (b) the description is outdated and effort/risk regressions need explicit detection and reporting? → **Answer (producer, 2026-08-23): "The goal is to prevent ping-pong — do what you need to." Interpreted as Reading A: effort/risk stay excluded from the merge lists (prevention by construction); the guard targets merge-participating fields (status/stage/priority/assignee) and reports protected effort/risk conflict attempts without importing them. Adding effort/risk to the merge is a non-goal.** Source: interactive reply, this intake session (2026-08-23).
- **Q**: What is the exact override flag name? The ACs mention `--accept-regressions` or equivalent. → **Flagged for producer confirmation.**
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS8XLS0Z00759QI** – Pi TUI tools.ts: smart selection (helper copy + fetch merge + apply) (completed)
- **WL-0MSVRMAWM007QNR5** – Downtime worker: parseLlamaStatus rejects numeric slot_id — every poll fail-closes to busy, zero dispatches (completed)
- **WL-0MSHWHFAK005WKDB** – [test-failure] defaultSettings has default browseItemCount of 10 — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches

# Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J)

## Headline

Flip the space priority in the Herdr worklist pane: the selection list may use up to the full available pane height (including its header lines), and the metadata section fills whatever space remains — expanding when the list is short, sitting below the fold (revealed by scrolling down) when the list is long — scrolling internally when its content overflows.

## Problem statement

The metadata section below the selection list currently reserves a fixed 20–40% of the pane height (`computeMetadataPanelHeight`), squeezing the list. When the list needs more vertical space than it is allotted, it scrolls and the header/top lines scroll off the top of the pane, even though the metadata section below is eating rows the list could use. The metadata section should no longer force the list to scroll off the top.

## Users

- **Herdr users (human and AI agent)** browsing the work item list in a pane, who want the selection list — including its header line — to use as much vertical space as it needs, up to the maximum available, so items don't scroll off the top prematurely.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, when the list is long, I want the list (header + items) to take up to the full pane height so I can see as many items as possible without the top scrolling off.
- As a Herdr user, when the list is short, I want the metadata section to expand into the leftover space so the pane still shows the selected item's metadata.
- As a Herdr user, when the list fills the full pane, I want to scroll the pane down to expose the rest of the list and then the metadata section, with the initial view starting at the top of the selection list.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **List takes as much space as it needs, up to the max available**: The selection list (header line + items + group separators + footer) can use up to the maximum number of vertical lines available in the pane (pane rows minus the reserved notification row). The metadata section no longer reserves a fixed 20–40% share that forces the list to scroll.
2. **Initial view at top**: When the list fills the full vertical space, the view starts at the top of the selection list (header + first items visible). Scrolling the pane down exposes the rest of the list and, at the end, the metadata section.
3. **Metadata fills the rest**: When the list content is shorter than the available height, the metadata section expands to fill the leftover space below the list.
4. **Metadata scrolls if necessary**: When the metadata content overflows the space allotted to it, it scrolls independently using the existing `m`/`M` keys and `metaScrollOffset` (with the existing `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator), and the selection-driven reset behaviour is preserved.
5. **No regression**: Keyboard navigation (arrows/j/k, PgUp/PgDn, g/G, wrap), stage filtering, group separators, auto-refresh, code-freeze banner, and the reserved notification row continue to work; rendered output never exceeds the pane's `rows` budget.
6. **Testing**: Unit tests cover (a) list height = min(content need, max available), (b) metadata expansion when the list is short, (c) reveal-by-scroll when the list fills the pane and initial view at top, (d) metadata scroll clamping under the new layout, and (e) the output line-count invariant (≤ `rows`).
7. **Docs**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** — managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Plugin-local change in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; no `wl` CLI or backend schema changes.
- The rendered output must never exceed the pane's `rows` budget (last row reserved for the notification line; group-separator accounting must not overflow) — the invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO must hold.
- Preserve existing keyboard bindings: `m`/`M` for metadata scrolling, and all list-navigation keys unchanged.
- Must compose with the description preview feature (WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3, in progress) which adds up to 3 preview lines to the metadata panel content.
- The metadata panel keeps a small minimum height (~3 rows) whenever it is rendered (short list or scrolled into view) so it remains usable, even if that means its content scrolls internally.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — document-flow layout**: the user's answers describe the list and metadata section as stacked content within one scrollable viewport (view starts at top; scrolling down reveals the rest of the list, then the metadata). An alternative pinned-footer layout (metadata always visible at the pane bottom) does not match the answers and is out of scope.
- **Assumption — header behavior**: "start the view at the top of the selection list" is interpreted as the initial render showing header + first items; the exact pin-vs-scroll behaviour of the header line during scroll is an implementation detail, but the header must be visible initially (matching the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO invariant that the header is never cut off).
- **Risk — line-count regression**: changing the list/metadata space split could reintroduce output overflowing the pane (the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO bug). Mitigation: keep the ≤ `rows` invariant as an explicit test.
- **Risk — metadata scroll clamping**: if the panel's allotted height changes dynamically, `metaScrollDown`'s clamp against content height must still hold; keep the existing clamp tests and update them for the new sizing.
- **Risk — scope creep**: "below the fold" indicators (WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ), mouse/touch scrolling (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ), and metadata panel content changes (WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7) are related but separate items — do not implement them here.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:
  - `computeMetadataPanelHeight(rows)` (lines ~85–119) — reserves a 20–40% share of pane rows for the metadata panel (min 3 rows), from WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X.
  - `WorkItemListState._listHeight()` (line ~681) — `max(3, rows - 4 - panelHeight)`; used by `_adjustScroll` and `getVisibleItems`.
  - `createListRenderer()` (line ~1830) — computes `panelHeight = computeMetadataPanelHeight(rows)`, `listArea = rows - 1 - panelHeight`, `listHeight = rows - 4 - panelHeight`; renders header + items + separators + fill + footer + metadata panel lines, clamped to `rows - 1`.
  - `formatMetadataPanel()` (line ~982) — renders exactly `panelRows` lines with independent scroll offset and `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator; `metaScrollDown` clamps against content height.
  - `metaScrollOffset` reset on selection change (`_resetMetaScroll`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `computeMetadataPanelHeight` responsive-ramp tests (lines ~1448), metadata scroll clamp tests (line ~1663), renderer line-count invariant tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — entry point wiring (render callback passes `metaScrollOffset`/`metaLastCommand`).

## Desired change

- In `createListRenderer()`: compute the list's space need from its content (header + banner + items + separators + footer), capped at the maximum available rows (`rows - 1` minus the notification budget). The metadata section is allotted the remainder: it expands to fill leftover space when the list is short, and when the list fills the pane it is positioned below the list content so scrolling down reveals the rest of the list and then the metadata section.
- Initial view starts at the top of the selection list (scroll offset 0 / header visible) even when the list is long.
- Keep `computeMetadataPanelHeight` (or replace its call sites) such that the fixed 20–40% reservation no longer forces the list to scroll; the metadata panel keeps a small minimum height (~3 rows) and scrolls internally via `metaScrollOffset`/`m`/`M` when its content overflows.
- Keep `formatMetadataPanel`'s independent-scroll contract (exactly `panelRows` lines) and the `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — list/metadata space split, initial view-at-top, metadata scroll clamping; primary change location.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — update responsive-ramp tests; add list-height/content-need, metadata-expansion, reveal-by-scroll, and line-count invariant tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — render callback wiring (`metaScrollOffset`, `metaLastCommand`), only if the space split needs state/context passed through.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** (completed) — introduced the metadata panel and the fixed 20–40% reservation this item reverses; its AC1 said the list "always keeps the majority of the space (≥60%)" — this item changes that priority.
- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** (in progress) — adds a description preview to the metadata panel (up to 3 lines), which makes the metadata content taller; this item must compose with it.
- **WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO** (completed) — the output line-count invariant (`≤ rows`) this item must preserve.
- **WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ** (open) — "no indication of items below the fold" — related scrolling UX; not required by this item but related.
- **WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7** (open) — drops the duplicate ID row from the metadata panel; touches the same `formatMetadataPanel` output.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When the list is long and fills the pane, should the metadata panel keep a small guaranteed minimum (e.g., ~3 rows, as today) so it stays visible and scrolls within that, or may it shrink all the way to zero (hidden)?" — Answer (user): "If the selection list takes up the full vertical space scrolling the pane down should expose the rest of the list and the meta-data section. However we should start the view at the top of the selection list." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: when the list fills the pane, the metadata section sits below the list content and is revealed by scrolling the pane down; the initial view starts at the top of the selection list (header visible). Research: inspected `computeMetadataPanelHeight` (20–40% fixed reservation) and the renderer's `listArea`/`listHeight` budget in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- Q2: "When the list has only a few items, should the list take only the rows it needs (header + items + separators + footer) and let the metadata panel expand to fill the leftover space, or should the list always occupy the full available height and the metadata panel stay at a fixed small size?" — Answer (user): "meta-data can expand to fill space." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: the list takes only what it needs when short; the metadata section expands into the leftover space.
- Q3: "Should the existing m/M metadata scrolling behavior stay as-is, just operating in the new (possibly smaller) panel space?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply. Research: `metaScrollOffset`, `_resetMetaScroll` on selection change, `metaScrollUp/Down` clamping and the `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator already exist in `worklist.ts`.

## Problem

`prefix+l` in herdr (→ `worklog-selection-list.open-podcast-editor-tab`) crashed immediately: the spawned worklist pane exited with code 1 within ~0.3s.

## Root cause

The pane runs `npx tsx src/index.ts`; the plugin crashed on startup with:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'marked' imported from .../packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts
```

`marked` (and the `@worklog/shared` file dependency) are declared in `packages/herdr/package.json` but were not installed. The root `npm run build` postbuild hook (`scripts/install-herdr.sh`) links the plugin and registers the prefix+l keybinding but never runs `npm install`, so a fresh clone (or a node_modules cleanup) leaves the plugin broken with a confusing 'crash on prefix+l' symptom.

## Fix

Ensure dependencies are installed as part of the plugin build. Options:
- Run `npm ci` (or `npm install`) in `packages/herdr` inside the `[[build]]` step or the root postbuild hook
- Verify the installed herdr plugin starts (`npx tsx src/index.ts`) after build

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Running `npm run build` at repo root from a clean clone installs `packages/herdr` dependencies
- [ ] `prefix+l` opens the Podcast Editing tab without the plugin crashing (pane stays alive)
- [ ] No duplicate work; existing install-herdr.sh behavior (idempotent link + keybinding insert) preserved

# Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election with shared coordination file

## Problem statement

The current Downtime Dispatcher has every herdr plugin instance polling the llama-proxy independently, using priority, round-robin, and jitter to share dispatch load. This approach still allows one instance to dominate dispatches and doesn't scale well when many instances are active. A leader-election model with a shared coordination file would simplify the dispatch logic: all instances contribute their most important work item to a shared list, one elected leader dispatches work from that list, and the coordination file acts as the single source of truth.

## Users

- **Operator running multiple herdr instances** — wants fair dispatch distribution without per-instance polling complexity; each instance contributes its worklog's most important item to a shared queue.
- **Operator with idle local LLM** — wants work dispatched efficiently: the leader polls for idle slots and pulls from the coordination list, removing dispatched items so others can re-queue.

### User stories

- As an operator running N herdr instances, each instance should automatically join a shared coordination list with its most important work item from its own worklog, identified by instance and worklog directory.
- As an operator, I want one elected leader to handle all LLM idle checks and dispatches, so the other instances don't waste cycles polling the proxy.
- As an operator, if the leader crashes, another instance should automatically take over within 5 minutes.
- As an operator, when the leader dispatches an item, that item is removed from the coordination list and the instance that owned it will add a new item on its next 30-minute check-in.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Leader election** — Instances use a file lock to elect a single leader; the first instance to acquire the lock wins. If no leader is elected (lock unavailable), the instance continues operating without dispatching.
2. **Lease-based leadership** — The leader holds a 5-minute lease, refreshed every time it polls the llama-proxy. If the lease expires (leader crashed or idle), instances detect the expiry and run a new election.
3. **Coordination file** — A shared JSON file at `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.json` stores one entry per instance: `{instanceId, workItemId, directory, assignedAt, lastUpdated}`. Each instance:
   - On startup and every 30 minutes, reads the coordination file
   - If it has an entry, verifies its work item is still its most important; if not, updates the entry
   - If no entry exists, adds its most important item to the list
   - If its entry was removed (by leader dispatch), adds a new entry on the next check-in
4. **Leader dispatch logic** — The leader reads the coordination file, determines priority order (audit tier first, then implement, then plan, then intake), checks LLM idle status (same 30s proxy poll + 4 min continuous idle threshold), and dispatches the highest-priority available item when a slot opens. The dispatched item is removed from the coordination file.
5. **Multi-worklog support** — Each instance operates on its own worklog directory (identified in the coordination file). The leader compares work items across directories using the standard tier priority system.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Single-machine only for v1** — coordination file access uses flock; no cross-machine support in this version.
- **30-minute check-in interval** — instances update the coordination file every 30 minutes (first check-in on startup).
- **5-minute lease** — leader lease timeout is 5 minutes, refreshed on each proxy poll cycle.
- **Fail-safe** — missing/unreadable coordination file or failed leader election degrades to current behavior (no dispatch from that instance).
- **Existing dispatch guard preserved** — the dispatched-marker exclusion and CAS claim mechanisms continue to prevent double-dispatch.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` runs tiers in order: audit → implement → plan → intake.
- Each herdr instance polls the llama-proxy independently using fixed jittered intervals.
- Dispatch markers (`downtime-dispatches.log`) + CAS claim prevent double-dispatch.
- Coordination file concept doesn't exist; all state is instance-local.
- Key files: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **Leader election module** — New file (`leader-election.ts`) implementing file-lock-based leader election with lease management. Leader refreshes lease on each proxy poll; lease expiry triggers re-election.
2. **Coordination file module** — New file (`coordination.ts`) managing the shared coordination JSON file. Each instance reads/writes its entry; entries contain instanceId, workItemId, worklog directory, and timestamps.
3. **Refactored dispatch worker** — Leader-only dispatch logic reads the coordination file, applies tier priority, checks LLM idle, dispatches the highest-priority item, and removes it. Non-leader instances skip proxy polling and dispatch; they only update their coordination entry on the 30-minute check-in.
4. **Updated scheduler** — Non-leader instances use a 30-minute check-in timer for coordination updates; the leader uses the existing proxy-poll cadence (30s) for LLM idle checks plus coordination updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — NEW: File-lock leader election with lease management (TTL, expiry detection, re-election).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — NEW: Shared coordination file read/write (flock, JSON format, entry management).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Refactored: leader checks before dispatch, coordination file integration, tier priority from list.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — May need minor updates to record coordination-file operations alongside dispatches.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Updated: scheduler wiring for leader vs. non-leader timers.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — May need updates for the 30-minute check-in cadence on non-leader instances.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Wire coordination file path and leader election into `createDowntimeDeps`.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6** — Downtime dispatcher: priority-first selection with round-robin tie-break (open) — this refactoring **supersedes** the round-robin/jitter approach; that work item should be closed or marked absorbed. This relationship should be recorded as a blocker/absorbed link.
- **WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN** — Downtime dispatcher: conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion (completed) — CAS/claim infrastructure this builds on.
- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — Log herdr downtime dispatches (completed) — dispatch log pattern reused.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** Each instance operates on its own worklog directory, so "most important item" is computed independently per instance using the standard tier priority.
- **Assumption:** The coordination file is stored in a shared `.worklog/` directory accessible to all instances (local filesystem, not network storage in v1).
- **Risk:** Race conditions during coordination file writes (two instances updating simultaneously). Mitigation: flock on write; brief lock-hold (read-modify-write is fast JSON manipulation).
- **Risk:** Leader election race when multiple instances start simultaneously. Mitigation: file lock is atomic; one wins, others detect lock held and retry after a short backoff (e.g., 1-2 seconds).
- **Risk:** Stale entries from crashed instances linger in the coordination file until they expire or are cleaned up. Mitigation: include `lastUpdated` timestamp per entry; the leader can prune entries older than the lease timeout (5 min) on each dispatch cycle.
- **Risk:** Instance's worklog becomes inaccessible during a check-in (disk error, permission change). Mitigation: fail-open — skip the check-in for that instance, do not remove the entry, log the error.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Ensure the refactoring doesn't inadvertently break existing dispatch guard mechanisms (CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion). Extra opportunities (e.g., cross-machine support) are recorded as linked work items, not scope.
- **Risk:** 5-minute lease means up to 5 minutes of no dispatch if leader crashes. Acceptable for v1; could be reduced in a follow-up.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Leader election mechanism?" — Answer (user): "(a) Simple: first to acquire a file lock wins". Source: interactive reply.

# Exclude child items from audit-tier dispatch selection

## Problem statement

The audit-tier dispatch selects items from `completed` / `in_review` work items without a valid audit, but currently includes child items (sub-tasks) alongside parent items. Child items should never be dispatched independently — only parent items should appear in the audit dispatch tier.

## Users

- **Producers reviewing epics** — the completed/in_review review queue should contain parent items only, so the audit dispatch focuses on reviewing actual deliverable units, not sub-tasks.
- **Downtime dispatcher** — when dispatching `/skill:audit` during idle time, it should only spawn audits for parent items, never for children.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` uses `--root-only` on the `wl list` call so that only items without a parent are returned as audit candidates.
2. All existing audit-tier tests pass with the change (candidates should be unaffected unless they are children, which should now be excluded).
3. If a test or scenario creates child items in `completed`/`in_review`, those children are never returned as audit candidates.
4. Documentation updated: code comments in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` reflecting the root-only constraint; README downtime section updated.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- This is a minimal surgical change: only the `wl list` arguments in `getNextAuditCandidate` need modification (add `--root-only`).
- No changes to the implement-tier selection are in scope — that tier uses `wl next`, which already respects parent-child hierarchy (per completed items WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1 and WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR).

## Existing state

- `getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` calls:
  ```
  wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json
  ```
- `wl list` supports a `--root-only` flag that shows only items without a parent.
- Parent-child hierarchy was already addressed in `wl list` (WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR) and `wl next` (WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1, WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1).

## Desired change

Add `--root-only` to the `wl list` call in `getNextAuditCandidate`:
```
wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json
```

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getNextAuditCandidate` function (line ~405): add `--root-only` to `buildWlArgs` call.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — interface doc comment for `getNextAuditCandidate` may need updating to reflect root-only contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — audit selection tests may need a test confirming children are excluded.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — downtime section (update if documenting selection rules).

## Related work

- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr) — introduces `--root-only` flag on `wl list`.
- **WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1** — wl next should return parent items instead of surfacing children individually — ensures `wl next` returns parents, not children.
- **WL-0MSI9WPNI0044RL8** — Audit dispatch tier — establishes the audit tier concept.
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** — Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit — audit tier wiring.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY** — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions — parent for audit-tier dispatched-marker exclusion.
- **WL-0MSLUASNF001LLAT** — Dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection — child of above.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** If existing tests create child items in `completed`/`in_review`, they were previously valid candidates and now will be excluded — test fixtures may need updating to use root items.
- **Risk:** If ALL `completed`/`in_review` items happen to be children (extremely rare), the audit tier returns no candidates — this is the correct behavior (no root items to audit).
- **Assumption:** `--root-only` does not change the JSON output shape — verified against `wl list --help` (it is a filter flag, not a format modifier).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Implement-tier selection (`wl next`) already respects parent-child hierarchy (per WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1); no changes needed there. If implement-tier also needs explicit `--root-only`, that is a separate work item.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Does this apply to the implement tier as well?" — Answer (operator): Only the audit tier is in scope. The implement tier (`wl next`) already returns parent items instead of children (WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1). — Source: interactive reply.
